actuator_details: Classifies human hand grasps into **6 fundamental types**: (1) cylindrical, (2) tip, (3) hook, (4) palmar, (5) spherical, (6) lateral. Schlesinger's taxonomy was developed for designing WWI-veteran prosthetic hands and remains the foundational reference for grasp classification 100+ years later. **Predates and underlies all modern grasp taxonomies** (Cutkosky 1989, Iberall 1986, Feix 2014).
control_architecture: N/A — taxonomy / classification framework.
creator: Georg Schlesinger (TU Berlin)
disclosure_citation: Schlesinger, G. 'Der Mechanische Aufbau der Künstlichen Glieder' [The Mechanical Construction of Artificial Limbs]. In Borchardt, M. et al. (eds.) 'Ersatzglieder und Arbeitshilfen für Kriegsbeschädigte und Unfallverletzte', Springer Berlin 1919. The foundational post-WWI prosthetic-hand mechanical-design treatise, written by Georg Schlesinger of TU Berlin.
notable_capabilities: 6 fundamental grasp types (cylindrical, tip, hook, palmar, spherical, lateral)
underlies all modern grasp taxonomies (Cutkosky 1989, Feix 2014)
foundational text for post-WWI prosthetic-hand design
prior_art_notes: Schlesinger's 1919 6-grasp classification is the foundational post-WWI grasp-taxonomy public-domain prior art. **106-year-deep public-domain anchor** for any commercial humanoid claim on grasp categorization. actuator_details: Mathematical transformation: maps three-phase stator currents (a, b, c) of a synchronous machine to a rotating reference frame (d, q, 0). The d-axis aligns with the rotor, q-axis is 90° offset, 0-axis is zero-sequence. This transformation makes the equivalent inductances constant (vs. time-varying in the abc frame), enabling tractable control synthesis.
control_architecture: mathematical foundation for FOC (Field-Oriented Control) of brushless DC and AC servo motors, which is the universal modern motor-control architecture for humanoid actuators
creator: Robert H. Park
disclosure_citation: Park, Robert H. 'Two-reaction theory of synchronous machines — generalized method of analysis — Part I'. AIEE Transactions 48(3): 716-727, July 1929.
notable_capabilities: mathematical foundation for vector control of electrical machines
universal underlying transformation for AC and BLDC servo control
prior_art_notes: Park's 1929 transformation is the mathematical foundation underlying FOC (Field-Oriented Control) of every modern brushless DC and AC servo motor in humanoid platforms. Anticipates with 97 years of prior art: (1) the dq0 reference-frame transformation as the basis for vector control — every modern humanoid actuator controller (Moteus, ODrive, SimpleFOC, T-Motor, plus closed proprietary controllers) uses this transformation; (2) the decoupling of torque-producing and flux-producing current components — foundational for any motor-control humanoid IP. Modern claims on FOC implementations in humanoid actuators all face this 97-year academic prior art.
sensing: none directly; downstream FOC requires rotor-position feedback
sources: Park, R.H. 'Two-reaction theory of synchronous machines, Part I'. AIEE Trans. 48(3): 716-727, 1929.
Park, R.H. 'Two-reaction theory of synchronous machines, Part II'. AIEE Trans. 52(2): 352-355, 1933.
Krause, P.C., Wasynczuk, O., Sudhoff, S.D. Analysis of Electric Machinery and Drive Systems (textbook lineage).

actuator_details: Cycloidal speed reducer: an eccentric-driven cycloid disk meshes with internal pin teeth, producing high-ratio gear reduction (typically 6:1 to 119:1) in a compact axial form factor. Two-cycloid 180-degree opposed disks balance the eccentric motion. Backlash typically <1 arc-minute due to multi-tooth contact (vs. single-tooth contact in spur gears).
control_architecture: purely mechanical reducer; integrates with motor + servo controller
creator: Lorenz Bayer-Ehrlich (inventor, Germany); Sumitomo Heavy Industries (commercial development, Japan)
disclosure_citation: Lorenz Bayer-Ehrlich. German patent DE745552 (1937) for cycloidal speed reducer. Commercial production: Sumitomo Heavy Industries, CYCLO drive product line, 1937 onwards.
prior_art_notes: Sumitomo CYCLO is the foundational academic and industrial disclosure of cycloidal speed reducers in robotic actuators. Anticipates with full mechanism specificity, dating to 1937: (1) cycloid-disk-and-pin-tooth gear reduction for high-ratio compact actuators — relevant to *every* modern humanoid claim using cycloidal reducers (Apptronik Apollo, Sanctuary Phoenix, Boston Dynamics Atlas G3, multiple Chinese commodity humanoids); (2) two-disk 180-degree opposed cycloid arrangement for vibration cancellation — relevant to claims on balanced cycloidal joints; (3) low-backlash multi-tooth meshing — relevant to backlash-control IP. The 1937 German patent has long since expired; CYCLO products have been continuously sold since 1937 with full mechanism documentation. Modern cycloidal humanoid actuator claims (the corpus's pre-this-entry chain only had 3 entries from 2023) face this 89-year industrial-academic anchor as 102 prior art at extraordinary depth.
sources: Sumitomo Heavy Industries CYCLO drive product literature (multiple decades).
Lehmann, M. and Schreiber, R. 'Improved Cycloidal Speed Reducer'. ASME Mechanisms Conference, 1992.
Litvin, F.L. Gear Geometry and Applied Theory. Cambridge University Press, 2004 (standard reference covering cycloidal kinematics).

actuator_details: **The first crewed vessel to the deepest point on Earth** (Challenger Deep, 10,916 m, 23 Jan 1960). Bathyscaphe architecture: gasoline-filled float (lighter than water) for positive buoyancy; iron-shot ballast for descent control; steel pressure sphere ('cabin') for crew. No active propulsion for descent — gravity + ballast drop. The foundational free-buoyancy crewed deep-ocean architecture. Don Walsh (US Navy) + Jacques Piccard (Swiss) made the dive.

actuator_details: **Pneumatic artificial muscle**: an inflatable inner bladder encased in a braided helical shell. When pressurized, the bladder expands radially and the braided shell shortens axially, producing **contraction-and-tension** that mimics biological muscle. Contraction ratio 25-30%, force-to-weight >1 kN/kg. The architectural parent of all braided-shell pneumatic actuators in modern soft robotics (Festo Fluidic Muscle, Shadow Air Muscle, Pisa-IIT McKibben-actuated platforms).
control_architecture: Pneumatic pressure-driven; inherently compliant (gas-spring behavior); typically actuated against an antagonistic muscle pair for bidirectional control.
creator: Joseph L. McKibben (NIH, Bethesda)
disclosure_citation: McKibben, J. L. (1957). Pneumatic artificial muscle developed at the National Institutes of Health for an orthotic device for polio patients. The original technical reports describe the braided-shell pneumatic actuator that contracts when pressurized. Subsequently extensively studied — Daerden + Lefeber 'Pneumatic Artificial Muscles: actuators for robotics and automation' European Journal of Mechanical and Environmental Engineering 47(1) 2002 is a canonical academic survey.
notable_capabilities: high force-to-weight (>1 kN/kg) at low cost
prior_art_notes: The McKibben pneumatic artificial muscle is the canonical compliant-actuator foundation of soft robotics. 68-year-deep public-domain prior art (1957). The architectural parent of: Festo Fluidic Muscle (round-16 entry below), Shadow Robot Air Muscle, Pisa-IIT McKibben-actuated humanoid platforms (e.g., Walk-Man's compliant-joint design), Pneubotics. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on pneumatic-actuated compliant motion or biologically-mimetic actuator design. Particularly relevant if free-humanoid-platform pivots toward a soft-humanoid v0.2 variant — the pneumatic-actuator branch is well-anticipated.

Daerden, F., Lefeber, D. 'Pneumatic Artificial Muscles' EJMEE 47(1) 2002 — canonical academic survey.
Tondu, B. 'Modelling of the McKibben artificial muscle' J. Intelligent Material Systems 23(3) 2012.

The Kalman filter underlies every IMU-based attitude estimator + every GPS-INS-DVL fusion stack in the corpus.

The mechanism that pre-dates and prefigures every modern anthropomorphic prosthetic + dexterous research hand. Belgrade-USC Hand (~1988) refined version at USC under George Bekey.

actuator_details: Originally six 1.5 kW electric thrusters in vectored arrangement; upgraded to high-efficiency rim-driven brushless thrusters in the 2013 Personnel Sphere upgrade. Variable-buoyancy via syntactic-foam main body (positive buoyancy) plus variable-ballast trim tank (active trim). Two seven-function manipulator arms (Schilling Robotics or Kraft Telerobotics in current configuration).
control_architecture: Manned operation by 1 pilot + 2 observers in titanium pressure sphere (2-inch wall, 4500 m depth rating since 1973 hull replacement; Ti-6Al-4V since 2013 sphere upgrade). Thruster commands via joystick; manipulator via dedicated master controllers. No autonomy — every motion is a human command. The control architecture's value to the corpus is demonstrating that bimanual underwater dexterous manipulation has been a solved operational problem at depth since the 1960s.
creator: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution / Allyn Vine concept (1956); General Mills Mechanical Division built v1
disclosure_citation: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. DSV Alvin operational since June 1964; first published 4500 m dive Aug 1973. Extensive academic publication record via WHOI deep-submergence vehicle group: Ballard 1985 (Titanic dives), Yoerger et al. mission reports 1991+, Kohnen ed. 'Manned Submersibles' (1978). Operational and design details in the public domain via U.S. Navy / WHOI.

notable_capabilities: bimanual master-slave manipulation since first deployment
found USS Thresher debris (1964-65), explored Titanic (1986), HMS Hood

prior_art_notes: DSV Alvin is the foundational manned deep-submergence vehicle. Its 60-year operational record establishes essentially every architectural element of modern submersible robotics as long-anticipated prior art: titanium pressure-hull design at 4500 m+ depth (1973), syntactic-foam buoyancy matched to depth pressure, variable-ballast trim tanks, vectored-thruster station-keeping, master-slave manipulator pairs for sample collection. Directly shields free-humanoid-submersible commitments on: 50 m pressure hull (62 years deeper than Alvin's 1964 baseline), 8-thruster vectored layout (the 6-thruster Alvin pattern is the lower bound), bimanual manipulator architecture (Alvin's Schilling/Kraft 7-function arms are the ROV-class equivalent of the bipedal upper body). Any commercial humanoid AUV claim on these elements faces a 62-year-deep public-domain academic lineage with extensive WHOI publication.

actuator_details: **The foundational 6-DoF parallel mechanism**. 6 prismatic actuators connecting a fixed base to a moving platform via ball joints. Provides full 6-DoF motion (3 translation + 3 rotation). The antecedent (Gough 1947 / Dunlop) was the first production application — universal tire test rig. Stewart's 1965 paper formalized the kinematic theory. **The architectural anchor of**: every flight simulator, every motion-base (Disney/Universal rides), every 6-DoF haptic device (round-18 Phantom), every parallel-kinematic machine tool.

Mosher's 1968 SAE paper discloses with full specificity: (1) hydraulic actuation per leg with 3-DOF — anticipates hydraulic legged claims by Boston Dynamics (BigDog 2005) by 37 years; (2) master-slave kinesthetic teleoperation with force feedback — anticipates teleoperation claims for legged systems; (3) 1500 kg payload legged loadbearing — anticipates legged-loadbearing claims (Boston Dynamics LS3, Ghost Robotics Vision 60); (4) 90 hp combustion engine power source for legged locomotion. actuator_details: Theoretical framework introduced for synthesis of bipedal gait. ZMP defined as the point on the support polygon where the net moment of inertial and gravitational forces has zero horizontal component. Originally validated on early Belgrade exoskeletons.
control_architecture: Bipedal gait synthesis constrained by ZMP-inside-support-polygon: trajectory generation guarantees dynamic stability if ZMP remains within the convex hull of foot-ground contact at all times. Foundational stability criterion for actuated bipedal locomotion.
creator: Miomir Vukobratović and D. Juričić, Mihajlo Pupin Institute, Belgrade
disclosure_citation: Vukobratović, Miomir and Juričić, D. 'Contribution to the synthesis of biped gait.' IEEE Transactions on Bio-Medical Engineering BME-16(1): 1-6, January 1969. Earlier conference: Vukobratović, M. and Juričić, D. 'Contribution to the synthesis of biped gait.' Proc. IFAC Symposium on Technical and Biological Problems of Control, Yerevan, 1968.
prior_art_notes: Vukobratović's 1969 ZMP formulation is the foundational academic disclosure of dynamic-stability criteria for bipedal walking. Predates Honda P2 (1996) by 27 years and predates every modern humanoid bipedal patent at extraordinary depth. Anticipates with mathematical specificity: (1) the ZMP constraint as a sufficient condition for non-tipping bipedal gait — directly relevant to virtually every bipedal walking patent filed since 1990 (Honda, Sony, Toyota, every Asian humanoid program); (2) gait synthesis by ZMP-trajectory planning — relevant to claims on humanoid walking pattern generators (HRP series, ASIMO, NAO all use ZMP-derived planners); (3) the support polygon as the safety region for COM projection — relevant to claims on bipedal balance recovery. Heavily cited (>5000 citations); the ZMP concept has 13 books and several hundred papers as direct extensions. 57-year-deep 102 anchor against any bipedal-stability patent.
sources: Vukobratović, M. and Juričić, D. 'Contribution to the synthesis of biped gait.' IEEE Trans. BME-16(1): 1-6, 1969.
Vukobratović, M. and Borovac, B. 'Zero-moment point — thirty five years of its life.' Int. J. Humanoid Robotics 1(1): 157-173, 2004 (retrospective).

actuator_details: **The first fully automated robotic sample return from another celestial body**. Drill-and-store mechanism in lander; ascender stage rocketed back to Earth carrying 101g sealed sample. 35 cm core drilled into lunar regolith. Subsequent: Luna 20 (1972) + Luna 24 (1976; deepest robotic core sample on Moon at 2 m). The architectural predicate for OSIRIS-REx + Hayabusa + Chang'e-5/6 sample-return missions.

actuator_details: **The first operational extraterrestrial rovers**. Lunokhod 1 (1970): 8-wheel pressurized-hub chassis with convex lid. Solar-charged batteries + radioisotope nighttime heater. Teleoperated from Earth by 5-person crew with multi-second latency. Lunokhod 1: 322 days, 10.5 km. Lunokhod 2 (1973): improved cameras; 39 km traverse held the off-world drive distance record until Opportunity (2014). The architectural predicate for every subsequent planetary rover.
control_architecture: Earth-teleoperation with multi-second latency; 5-person crew.
creator: Lavochkin Association (USSR Academy of Sciences); Soviet space program
disclosure_citation: Lavochkin Association (USSR Academy of Sciences). Lunokhod 1 landed Mare Imbrium November 17, 1970. Lunokhod 2 landed Le Monnier crater January 15, 1973. The first operational extraterrestrial rovers.

prior_art_notes: Lunokhod 1 + 2 (Lavochkin 1970, 1973) are the first operational extra-terrestrial rovers. 55-year-deep public-domain prior art.

actuator_details: **The dominant assembly-robot architecture worldwide**. SCARA = Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm. 4-DoF: two horizontal-plane revolute joints (shoulder + elbow) + vertical prismatic joint + wrist rotation. Stiff vertically, compliant horizontally — ideal for assembly insertion tasks. Productized 1981 by Sankyo Seiki / Pentel / NEC. Now the dominant assembly-arm architecture: Epson (round-45) is the global SCARA volume leader; FANUC, Yaskawa, ABB, KUKA all make SCARA variants.
canonical_name: Makino SCARA (Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm)
control_architecture: 4-DoF closed-form kinematics; high-speed pick-and-place.

disclosure_citation: Makino, H. et al. SCARA architecture developed at University of Yamanashi 1978-1981 in consortium with 13 Japanese companies. Productized by Sankyo Seiki, Pentel, and NEC starting 1981. Hiroshi Makino (Yamanashi University) is the inventor.

actuator_details: **The foundational selective-compliance manipulator architecture**. 4-DoF arm: 2 horizontal revolute joints + 1 vertical prismatic + 1 wrist rotation. **Selectively compliant** in the horizontal plane (passive give) but stiff vertically — ideal for vertical-insertion assembly tasks. The dominant industrial-arm class for electronics assembly globally; >100,000 SCARA robots deployed in commercial manufacturing.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure for arbitrary serial-chain manipulators. Recursive forward-and-backward Lagrangian formulation reducing the per-DOF computational cost from O(n⁴) (Uicker-Kahn 1969) to O(n³), with explicit operation-counts for n=6 manipulators tabulated against Newton-Euler (Luh-Walker-Paul 1980) alternatives.
control_architecture: not a controller; the canonical efficient formulation of computed-torque inverse-dynamics for real-time control. Direct precursor to Featherstone's spatial-vector recursive Newton-Euler (1983-1987).
creator: John M. Hollerbach, MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Hollerbach, John M. 'A Recursive Lagrangian Formulation of Manipulator Dynamics and a Comparative Study of Dynamics Formulation Complexity.' IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics SMC-10(11): 730-736, November 1980.
notable_capabilities: practical real-time computed-torque feasibility for n=6 arms
prior_art_notes: Hollerbach 1980 is the canonical academic disclosure of efficient recursive Lagrangian manipulator dynamics, alongside Luh-Walker-Paul 1980 Newton-Euler. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on real-time computed-torque inverse-dynamics for humanoid arms — Hollerbach's O(n³) recursion is the basis for every embedded humanoid arm controller since the early 1980s; (2) claims on per-link recursive computation enabling distributed/parallel inverse-dynamics — Hollerbach's structure is explicitly recursive forward-and-backward; (3) the comparative-complexity tabulation enabling design-time formulation selection. >2500 citations; IEEE TSMC archive openly indexed. Lineage runs forward to Featherstone spatial-vector algebra (existing corpus entry) and Articulated-Body Algorithms. Modern humanoid arm-dynamics IP claims face this 46-year-deep anchor.
sources: Hollerbach, J. M. 'A Recursive Lagrangian Formulation of Manipulator Dynamics.' IEEE TSMC SMC-10(11): 730-736, 1980.
Luh, J. Y. S., Walker, M. W., Paul, R. P. 'On-line computational scheme for mechanical manipulators.' ASME J. Dyn. Sys. 102(2): 69-76, 1980 (companion Newton-Euler).

actuator_details: Foundational dynamic-legged-robot research program. Hydraulic actuators with passive springs (Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum / SLIP model). Three-part Raibert decomposition: hop-height control (vertical), forward-velocity control (foot placement), body-attitude control (hip torque). Each control axis independently solvable, enabling stable dynamic locomotion at a time (1983-1995) when the field was dominated by ZMP statically-stable walking.
canonical_name: Raibert MIT Leg Lab (foundational dynamic legged locomotion)
control_architecture: Three-part Raibert decomposition: vertical / horizontal / attitude control. Each axis solved independently; remarkably effective in practice. The conceptual ancestor of every modern dynamic-legged-robot controller.
creator: MIT Leg Laboratory; Marc Raibert (founder), then Jerry Pratt + Hugh Herr (post-Raibert era)
disclosure_citation: Raibert, M. H. 'Legged Robots That Balance'. MIT Press 1986. MIT Leg Lab (founded by Raibert at CMU 1981, moved to MIT 1986). Series of foundational dynamic-legged-robot designs: 3D one-leg hopper (1983), 3D quadruped (1984), planar biped (1989), 3D biped (1989), 4-legged Spring Flamingo (1995), Spring Turkey, M2, etc. Foundational predecessors of Boston Dynamics (Raibert founded BD 1992, took the Leg Lab portfolio with him). The corpus already has `raibert-hopping-1leg` for the foundational 1-leg hopper; this entry covers the broader Leg Lab portfolio as a corpus anchor.
notable_capabilities: foundational predecessor of Boston Dynamics (1992 founding portfolio)
MIT Press 1986 'Legged Robots That Balance' book

prior_art_notes: Marc Raibert's MIT Leg Lab portfolio (1981-1995) is the canonical foundational dynamic-legged-robotics academic anchor. 44-year-deep public-domain prior art predating the entire commercial humanoid era. **Most modern Boston Dynamics IP descends architecturally from this era** — Raibert founded BD in 1992 with the Leg Lab portfolio. The Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum (SLIP) model and Raibert's 3-part control decomposition remain the foundational analytical tools for dynamic legged locomotion. Together with Vukobratović ZMP (1969), McGeer passive walker (1990), Collins-Ruina passive (2005), establishes the four-pillar academic chain underpinning all modern bipedal/quadrupedal robotics — anticipating commercial humanoid claims by 30-55 years. Direct shielding for any commercial dynamic-locomotion claim. Note: corpus already has `raibert-hopping-1leg` for the specific 1-leg hopper; this entry is the broader Leg Lab portfolio anchor.
sources: Raibert, M. H. 'Legged Robots That Balance'. MIT Press 1986.

actuator_details: Algorithm: estimates optical flow (apparent pixel motion) between consecutive image frames by linearizing the brightness-constancy assumption locally and solving a least-squares system per pixel neighborhood. Iterative refinement extends to large displacements via image pyramid (KLT — Kanade-Lucas-Tomasi tracker, 1991 extension by Tomasi).
control_architecture: visual servoing primitive: optical flow → ego-motion estimate or scene-motion estimate → control input. Foundational for SLAM, visual odometry, object tracking in robotic perception.
creator: Bruce D. Lucas and Takeo Kanade, Carnegie Mellon University
disclosure_citation: Lucas, Bruce D. and Kanade, Takeo. 'An iterative image registration technique with an application to stereo vision'. Proceedings of the 7th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI), Vancouver, August 1981, pp. 674-679.
prior_art_notes: Lucas-Kanade 1981 is the foundational academic disclosure of dense optical flow estimation for robotic vision. Anticipates with 45 years of prior art: (1) optical-flow-based visual servoing for humanoid manipulation and locomotion — relevant to claims on visual-tracking-based humanoid policies; (2) iterative least-squares formulation that extends to modern KLT and PWC-style optical flow networks; (3) image-pyramid for multi-scale flow estimation. The KLT tracker is essentially the universal default for visual feature tracking and underlies SLAM, visual odometry, and many manipulation control loops. Modern visual humanoid IP all face this 1981 academic anchor.
sources: Lucas, B.D. and Kanade, T. 'An iterative image registration technique'. IJCAI 1981.
Tomasi, C. and Kanade, T. 'Detection and tracking of point features'. CMU Tech Report CMU-CS-91-132, 1991.
Bouguet, J.-Y. 'Pyramidal implementation of the affine Lucas Kanade feature tracker'. OpenCV documentation, 1999-2024.

prior_art_notes: Canadarm (Spar / NRC 1981+) is the foundational space robotic arm. 44-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: Three-fingered hand, 9 DOF (3 per finger), tendon-driven via N+1 cable architecture (4 cables per 3-DOF finger, antagonistic preload). DC motor bank in forearm; cables routed through pulleys at each joint. Fingertip force-torque sensors.
control_architecture: Stiffness control of grasp matrix; analytic force-closure analysis for grasp planning; kinematic analysis of fingertip task workspace. First systematic disclosure of grasp matrix G and grip Jacobian J_h.
creator: J. Kenneth Salisbury, Stanford University and JPL
disclosure_citation: Salisbury, J. Kenneth. 'Kinematic and Force Analysis of Articulated Hands.' PhD Thesis, Stanford University, May 1982. Companion paper: Salisbury, J.K. and Craig, J.J. 'Articulated hands: Force control and kinematic issues.' International Journal of Robotics Research 1(1): 4-17, March 1982.
end_effector: three-fingered articulated hand with active fingertip force control
prior_art_notes: Salisbury's 1982 thesis is the foundational academic disclosure of dexterous tendon-driven multi-finger hands with analytic grasp planning. Anticipates with mechanism-level specificity: (1) N+1 antagonistic tendon architecture for fingers — directly relevant to claims on tendon-driven humanoid hand actuators (Tesla Optimus hand, Figure hand, 1X hand); (2) the grasp matrix G and grip Jacobian formalism — anticipates virtually every modern grasp-planning patent; (3) force-closure analysis for grasp synthesis — relevant to grasp-search IP; (4) per-finger stiffness control — relevant to compliant-grasp claims. Salisbury later co-developed the PHANToM haptic device using the same kinematic framework. Thesis publicly available through Stanford Libraries; the IJRR companion paper has >2000 citations. 44-year-deep 102 anchor.

actuator_details: Single pneumatic-piston leg with hip joint for fore-aft balance; planar (2D) constrained motion. Pneumatic spring leg with active hip-position control. The leg compresses on landing and extends to provide thrust.
control_architecture: three-part decoupled control: (1) hopping height regulated by leg-spring extension during stance; (2) forward velocity regulated by foot-placement during flight; (3) body attitude regulated by hip torque. The decoupling is the disclosure.

disclosure_citation: Raibert, Marc H. 'Hopping in legged systems — modeling and simulation for the two-dimensional one-legged case'. IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics SMC-14(3): 451-463, May/June 1984. Earlier: Raibert, M.H. and Brown, H.B. 'Experiments in balance with a 2D one-legged machine'. Trans. ASME, J. Dyn. Sys., Meas., Cont., 106:75-81, 1984.

prior_art_notes: Raibert's hoppers are the foundational academic disclosure of dynamic legged balance and reduced-order-model control. The three-part decoupling (leg height / foot placement / body attitude) is the *exact* control architecture used by every subsequent dynamic-legged academic and commercial system, from Cassie to Atlas to MIT Mini Cheetah. Modern claims on reduced-order-model legged control all face Raibert's 1984 disclosure as 102 prior art. The 1985 book (Legged Robots that Balance, MIT Press) extends the disclosure to 2-legged and 4-legged versions and is one of the most-cited works in legged robotics. Publicly funded research; open publication.

actuator_details: Theoretical result: a continuous time-invariant feedback law that stabilizes a nonlinear system to an equilibrium must satisfy a specific topological condition. For systems that fail this condition (e.g. nonholonomic vehicles like wheeled cars and bipedal walkers near singular configurations), no continuous time-invariant stabilizing feedback exists. This necessitates time-varying or discontinuous control.
control_architecture: theoretical foundation for understanding limits of feedback stabilization in humanoid and mobile-robotic systems; directly motivates time-varying / discontinuous control architectures (LIPM walking, ZMP, switched-system bipedal)
creator: Roger W. Brockett, Harvard University
disclosure_citation: Brockett, Roger W. 'Asymptotic stability and feedback stabilization'. In Differential Geometric Control Theory (Brockett, Millman, Sussmann eds.), Birkhäuser, 1983, pp. 181-191.
notable_capabilities: foundational result for wheeled-robot and bipedal control theory
prior_art_notes: Brockett's 1983 condition is the theoretical foundation for understanding why certain humanoid and wheeled-robot systems cannot be stabilized with continuous time-invariant feedback. Modern claims on humanoid walking controllers, wheeled-balance controllers, and switched-system humanoid policies all rest on the design space Brockett's condition characterizes. Anticipates with 43 years of prior art: (1) theoretical justification for time-varying controllers in nonholonomic systems — relevant to wheeled-base humanoid IP; (2) the foundational characterization that motivates ZMP-based walking, LIPM-based walking, and modern reduced-order-model control. Heavily cited; canonical reference in nonlinear control textbooks.
sources: Brockett, R.W. 'Asymptotic stability and feedback stabilization'. Differential Geometric Control Theory, Birkhäuser, 1983.
Khalil, H. Nonlinear Systems (textbook reference for Brockett's condition).

actuator_details: **The foundational dexterous robotic hand**. Four fingers (three fingers + opposable thumb), 16 active DoF, tendon-driven by 32 remote pneumatic-piston actuators (push-pull tendons). Each finger has 4 DoF; thumb has 4 DoF. Hand-mounted directly on Utah/MIT teleoperator arm. Co-foundational with Salisbury Stanford-JPL Hand (corpus) of the entire dexterous-hand research field. Stephen Jacobsen subsequently founded Sarcos (corpus sarcos-guardian-xo-2018 lineage).
control_architecture: Decentralized PD joint control; teleoperation + autonomous-grasp research target.
creator: University of Utah Center for Engineering Design + MIT AI Lab; Stephen Jacobsen, John Wood, David Knutti, Klaus Biggers
disclosure_citation: Jacobsen, S.C., Wood, J.E., Knutti, D.F., Biggers, K.B. 'The Utah/MIT Dextrous Hand: Work in Progress'. International Journal of Robotics Research 3(4), Winter 1984. Joint project Center for Engineering Design (University of Utah) + MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.
notable_capabilities: 16 active DoF / 4 fingers / 32 pneumatic-piston tendon actuators
Utah CED + MIT AIL joint project
prior_art_notes: Utah/MIT Dextrous Hand (Jacobsen et al. IJRR 1984) is the foundational dexterous robotic hand. 41-year-deep public-domain prior art. Co-foundational with Salisbury Stanford-JPL Hand (corpus salisbury-stanford-jpl-hand) of the entire dexterous-hand research field. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim deriving from multi-finger tendon-driven anthropomorphic hands. Stephen Jacobsen lineage continues through Sarcos (corpus sarcos-guardian-xo-2018).
sources: Jacobsen, S.C. et al. 'The Utah/MIT Dextrous Hand'. IJRR 3(4), 1984.

actuator_details: **The first parallel pick-and-place delta robot**. Three (later 4 / 6) parallel arms in a triangular configuration; each arm has a parallelogram linkage that constrains the end-effector to translate without rotating. Extremely high speed (10+ picks/sec) for low-payload (<1 kg) pick-and-place. EPFL patent expired 2007; productized by ABB FlexPicker (round-45), Adept Quattro, FANUC M-1iA, Yaskawa MPP, Codian D5, etc. Defining architecture for food-processing + pharmaceutical high-speed packaging worldwide.
control_architecture: Parallel-mechanism inverse kinematics; high-speed servo control.

disclosure_citation: Clavel, R., Demaurex, M.-O. 'Delta, A Fast Robot with Parallel Geometry'. 18th International Symposium on Industrial Robots 1988; original patent 1985 (EP 0250470, expired 2007). EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, Switzerland). Commercialized 1987 via Demaurex SA (Romont, Switzerland; acquired by Bosch 1999, then to ABB ecosystem).
notable_capabilities: first parallel pick-and-place delta robot (EPFL patent 1985)
ancestor of ABB FlexPicker / Adept Quattro / FANUC M-1iA / etc.

Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim deriving from parallel delta-mechanism arms. Ancestor of ABB FlexPicker (round-45), Adept Quattro, and every commercial delta robot.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure: manipulability index w(q) = √det(J(q)Jᵀ(q)) and the manipulability ellipsoid in task space. Demonstrated on PUMA-class manipulators.
control_architecture: Redundancy resolution by maximizing manipulability gradient; configuration optimization for dexterous task execution; manipulability ellipsoid as design metric for manipulator topology.
creator: Tsuneo Yoshikawa, Kyoto University
disclosure_citation: Yoshikawa, Tsuneo. 'Manipulability of robotic mechanisms.' International Journal of Robotics Research 4(2): 3-9, June 1985. Earlier conference: Yoshikawa, T. 'Analysis and control of robot manipulators with redundancy.' First Int. Symp. on Robotics Research, MIT Press, 1984: 735-747.
prior_art_notes: Yoshikawa's manipulability formulation is the foundational academic disclosure of configuration-quality metrics and redundancy resolution for redundant manipulators. Anticipates: (1) manipulability-based redundancy resolution — directly relevant to claims on humanoid arm posture optimization (every dual-arm humanoid relies on a derivative); (2) the manipulability ellipsoid as a design and analysis tool — relevant to claims on optimization of humanoid arm/leg topology; (3) configuration-aware null-space optimization — relevant to whole-body humanoid posture control IP. Heavily cited (>5000 citations); standard reference in every robotics textbook. Modern humanoid arm-posture-optimization patents face this 40-year-deep 102 anchor.
sources: Yoshikawa, T. 'Manipulability of robotic mechanisms.' IJRR 4(2): 3-9, 1985.
Yoshikawa, T. Foundations of Robotics: Analysis and Control. MIT Press, 1990 (textbook consolidation).

actuator_details: Algorithmic and analytical disclosures for nonprehensile manipulation; demonstrated on standard CMU manipulators with pushers, fingers, and gripper jaws. The center-of-friction limit-surface formalism unifies pushing analysis.
control_architecture: Quasi-static analysis with friction-cone constraints; planning via mechanics-grounded action primitives; first formal treatment of nonprehensile manipulation (push-grasp, side-grasp, regrasp by pushing).
creator: Matthew T. Mason, Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute
disclosure_citation: Mason, Matthew T. 'Mechanics and planning of manipulator pushing operations.' International Journal of Robotics Research 5(3): 53-71, Fall 1986. Textbook consolidation: Mason, M.T. Mechanics of Robotic Manipulation. MIT Press, 2001. ISBN 0-262-13396-2.
end_effector: generic; covers pushing, sliding, pivoting, throwing, catching
prior_art_notes: Mason's pushing-mechanics work and 2001 textbook are the canonical academic disclosure of nonprehensile manipulation analysis. Mason 2001 is the standard graduate-level textbook for manipulation and is heavily cited (>3000 citations across the program). Modern 'learn-to-push' or 'learn-to-slide' manipulation patents face this 40-year-deep academic anchor.

actuator_details: Clinical scoring system for **thumb-opposition mobility** — an 11-point scale (0-10) rating the thumb-tip's ability to reach progressive landmarks across the hand (lateral side of index proximal phalanx through to base of little finger). Used clinically since 1986 for evaluating hand impairment + post-surgery rehabilitation. **The dominant clinical thumb-kinematics framework** — academically used to specify required ranges for prosthetic + robotic hands.

creator: Adalbert I. Kapandji (French orthopedic surgeon)

Annales de Chirurgie de la Main 5(1) 1986. Subsequent: Kapandji, A. I. 'The Physiology of the Joints, Volume 1: Upper Limb' (Churchill Livingstone, 6th ed. 2007 — the foundational hand-anatomy textbook in clinical use globally).

foundational reference for prosthetic + robotic hand design
anchors the kinematic specification for thumb opposition in modern dexterous hands

actuator_details: **Opposition-space theory of hand kinematics**: human grasps are structured around three fundamental opposition types — (1) **pad opposition** (thumb pad → finger pad), (2) **palm opposition** (thumb → palm + finger), (3) **side opposition** (thumb → lateral side of index finger). Any complex grasp is composed of these three primitives. The framework underlies **virtual-finger** modeling (multiple actual fingers acting as one virtual finger) which enables synergy-driven underactuated hand designs.
control_architecture: N/A — kinematic theory framework.
creator: Thea Iberall (UCSD; later USC); Michael Arbib (USC) collaboration
disclosure_citation: Iberall, T. 'Opposition Space as a Structuring Concept for the Analysis of Skilled Hand Movements'. In Heuer, H. + Fromm, C. (eds.) 'Generation and Modulation of Action Patterns', Springer 1986. Subsequent: Iberall, T., Bingham, G., Arbib, M. A. 'Opposition Space as a Structuring Concept for the Analysis of Skilled Hand Movements'. In Whiting, H.T.A. + Wing, A.M. (eds.) 'Themes in Motor Development', Springer 1986. UCSD + USC.
notable_capabilities: foundational reference for synergy-reduced underactuated hands
prior_art_notes: Iberall's 1986 opposition-space theory is the canonical academic framework for human grasp kinematics. 39-year-deep public-domain prior art for: 3-primitive opposition decomposition, virtual-finger modeling. **Directly underlies the Pisa-IIT SoftHand synergy reduction** (corpus entry pisa-iit-softhand): the SoftHand's single-DoF synergy maps onto Iberall's opposition primitives. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid hand claim on synergy-reduction or virtual-finger mechanism. Together with Schlesinger 1919 + Cutkosky 1989 (round-21 entries), establishes the academic-+-clinical-+-engineering grasp-taxonomy trio underlying all modern dexterous hand IP.

Featherstone's 2008 second edition (Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms, Springer) further consolidates. Continuously cited; baseline reference for all whole-body humanoid dynamics IP. Modern claims that 'compute humanoid joint torques via a recursive algorithm' face this 39-year-deep anchor.

actuator_details: Formal control framework, not a specific physical platform; demonstrated on PUMA-class and later Stanford manipulators. Operational-space inertia matrix Λ(x) = (J M⁻¹ Jᵀ)⁻¹ disclosed in closed form; task-space dynamic decoupling via the Jacobian-mass projection.
control_architecture: Operational-space (task-space) inverse dynamics: F = Λ(x) ẍ_d + μ + p, with null-space projection N = I - Jᵀ J̄ᵀ enabling redundancy resolution and multi-task hierarchies. Unified motion+force control via task-space impedance.

prior_art_notes: Khatib's 1987 operational-space formulation is the canonical academic disclosure of task-space inverse-dynamics control with null-space projection. actuator_details: **Variable-buoyancy propulsion** — no thrusters in primary propulsion. actuator_details: Unactuated bipedal mechanism. Knee-locked stance leg + free-swinging swing leg. Hip joint between legs. Walks down a shallow incline on gravity alone, no motors, no batteries, no sensors, no controller.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure for grasp planning. The Ferrari-Canny ε-metric is defined as the radius of the largest origin-centered ball contained in the grasp wrench space (convex hull of friction-cone-discretized contact wrenches).

disclosure_citation: Ferrari, Carlo and Canny, John. 'Planning optimal grasps.' IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation, Nice, France, May 1992: 2290-2295.

Anticipates: (1) wrench-space convex-hull grasp evaluation — directly relevant to virtually every grasp-planning patent filed since 2000 (DexNet, GraspNet, all academic and commercial grasp synthesizers cite Ferrari-Canny); (2) task-independent grasp ranking — relevant to claims on grasp-quality regression networks; (3) friction-cone-discretized wrench composition — relevant to grasp-mechanics IP. Heavily cited (>2500 citations). Modern data-driven grasp-quality networks (DexNet 2.0, GG-CNN, etc.) explicitly use Ferrari-Canny labels as ground truth — meaning every claim on grasp-quality-trained networks faces a 34-year-deep prior-art anchor. Publicly funded (NSF/Berkeley); openly published.

actuator_details: Compliant actuator with intentional mechanical spring placed in series between motor output and load. Bandwidth limited by spring stiffness; backdrivability and shock tolerance dramatically improved.

prior_art_notes: The Pratt-Williamson 1995 paper is the foundational academic disclosure of series-elastic actuators (SEA) — the dominant compliant-actuator architecture in legged and humanoid robotics. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) intentional series mechanical spring as the force-sensing element — directly relevant to claims on compliant humanoid actuators (Cassie, Digit, Apollo SEA derivatives); (2) spring-deflection-based force control without strain gauges — relevant to claims on encoder-only force feedback; (3) the bandwidth/stiffness tradeoff disclosure — anticipates SEA-design IP. Pratt's later commercial work (Yobotics, then Boston Dynamics' Atlas SEA) is grounded in this paper. Heavily cited (>3000 citations); SEA is now a textbook concept. 31-year-deep 102 anchor against any 'compliant humanoid actuator' patent.

IJCV 60(2): 91-110, 2004.
prior_art_notes: SIFT 1999 (and the canonical 2004 IJCV paper) is one of the most-cited algorithms in computer vision and a foundational visual-feature anchor for humanoid perception. actuator_details: Stability-indicator framework. The FRI point is defined as the point on the floor where the resultant ground-reaction force would have to act to maintain the foot in static equilibrium. Distinct from ZMP in that FRI can lie outside the support polygon when the foot is rotating.
control_architecture: Stability monitoring: when FRI exits the support polygon, the foot rotates and walking stability is lost; the FRI thereby provides a quantitative measure of how close the gait is to losing foot-flat contact. Generalizes ZMP to non-static-equilibrium foot conditions.
creator: Ambarish Goswami, INRIA Rhône-Alpes (later Honda Research Institute)
disclosure_citation: Goswami, Ambarish. 'Postural stability of biped robots and the foot-rotation indicator (FRI) point.' International Journal of Robotics Research 18(6): 523-533, June 1999.
notable_capabilities: graded measure of bipedal stability margin
prior_art_notes: Goswami's FRI is the canonical academic disclosure of an extended-ZMP stability indicator capable of quantifying impending foot-rotation. Anticipates: (1) graded stability metrics for bipedal walking that go beyond binary ZMP-inside/outside checks — relevant to claims on bipedal balance estimators in modern humanoids; (2) FRI as a continuous early-warning signal for tipping-onset — relevant to fall-prediction IP (every academic and commercial humanoid claiming 'fall prediction' or 'stability margin estimation' faces this); (3) the formal distinction between ZMP and FRI in non-quasi-static gaits — relevant to dynamic-walking control claims. Highly cited (>1000 citations); Goswami's later work at Honda Research Institute (Asimo group) extended this. 27-year-deep 102 anchor against bipedal-stability-monitoring IP.
sources: Goswami, A. 'Postural stability of biped robots and the FRI point.' IJRR 18(6): 523-533, 1999.

actuator_details: Demonstrated on MIT Leg Lab 'Spring Flamingo' planar bipedal walker with series-elastic actuators. Virtual mechanical elements (springs, dampers, virtual wheel) connected between body links and the world; their forces are computed and projected through joint Jacobians to motor torques.
control_architecture: Virtual Model Control: design intuitive virtual mechanical components (e.g., a virtual horizontal spring at the hip pulling the body forward, a virtual damper stabilizing pitch) and compute joint torques τ = Jᵀ F_virtual. Bypasses explicit ZMP planning; intuitive task-space control.
creator: Jerry Pratt, Chee-Meng Chew, Ann Torres, Peter Dilworth, Gill Pratt; MIT Leg Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Pratt, Jerry, Chew, Chee-Meng, Torres, Ann, Dilworth, Peter, Pratt, Gill. 'Virtual model control: An intuitive approach for bipedal locomotion.' International Journal of Robotics Research 20(2): 129-143, February 2001. Earlier: Pratt, J.E. and Pratt, G.A. 'Intuitive control of a planar bipedal walking robot.' IEEE ICRA 1998: 2014-2021.
prior_art_notes: Pratt's Virtual Model Control is a canonical alternative paradigm to ZMP for bipedal control, preserving compliance and intuitive task-space specification. Anticipates: (1) virtual-element-based humanoid torque control — directly relevant to claims on intuitive task-space bipedal controllers; (2) Jacobian-projected virtual force generation — relevant to whole-body humanoid IP that uses 'virtual' or 'imagined' references (every model-based controller for SEA-equipped humanoids descends from this); (3) integration with series-elastic compliance — relevant to compliant-humanoid claims. Pratt's 2000 PhD thesis ('Exploiting natural dynamics in the control of a planar bipedal walking robot,' MIT) extends the framework. Jerry Pratt later led IHMC's humanoid work (DRC Atlas, NASA Valkyrie controller). >1000 citations. 25-year-deep anchor against intuitive-bipedal-control patents.
sensing: joint position, foot ground contact, IMU
sources: Pratt, J. et al. 'Virtual model control.' IJRR 20(2): 129-143, 2001.
Pratt, J.E. PhD Thesis: 'Exploiting natural dynamics in the control of a planar bipedal walking robot.' MIT, 2000.

actuator_details: Reduced-order model: humanoid abstracted to a point mass at constant height connected to a CoP at the foot. The constant-height constraint linearizes the 3D dynamics into a 1D linear ODE per axis: ẍ = (g/h)(x - p_zmp). Closed-form solutions and preview-control-based pattern generators follow directly.
control_architecture: LIPM-based walking pattern generator: ZMP reference trajectory shaped by foot placement, CoM trajectory computed by preview control of the linearized ZMP-COM dynamics. Real-time tractable; basis for HRP-2/3/4/5P and most academic ZMP humanoids.
creator: Shuuji Kajita, Fumio Kanehiro, Kenji Kaneko, Kazuhito Yokoi, Hirohisa Hirukawa; AIST National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology, Japan
disclosure_citation: Kajita, Shuuji, Kanehiro, F., Kaneko, K., Yokoi, K., Hirukawa, H. 'The 3D Linear Inverted Pendulum Mode: A simple modeling for a biped walking pattern generation.' IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), Maui HI, October 29-November 3, 2001: 239-246.
notable_capabilities: reduced-order linear humanoid dynamics for real-time control
prior_art_notes: Kajita's 3D-LIPM is the canonical academic disclosure of real-time humanoid walking pattern generation via reduced-order model. Anticipates: (1) the LIPM ẍ = (g/h)(x - p) reduction — directly relevant to claims on real-time bipedal pattern generation in essentially every academic and commercial humanoid since 2001 (HRP series, NAO, ASIMO derivatives, Atlas-class, Optimus, Figure 02 all use LIPM-derivative real-time planners); (2) preview-control-based ZMP tracking (Kajita-Kanehiro 2003 ICRA paper extending this) — relevant to model-predictive bipedal walking IP; (3) the constant-height constraint as a real-time-tractable simplification — relevant to humanoid walking-controller claims. Heavily cited (>4000 citations between LIPM 2001 and preview-control 2003 papers). Basis for the textbook Kajita et al. 'Introduction to Humanoid Robotics' (Springer 2014).
sources: Kajita, S. et al. 'The 3D Linear Inverted Pendulum Mode.' IEEE/RSJ IROS 2001: 239-246.
Kajita, S. et al. 'Biped walking pattern generation by using preview control of zero-moment point.' IEEE ICRA 2003: 1620-1626.

actuator_details: Algorithmic framework: each motor primitive is a damped second-order linear ODE (point-attractor) plus a nonlinear forcing term f(s) that encodes the demonstrated trajectory shape. The forcing term is parameterized as a weighted sum of basis functions and learned from a single demonstration via locally-weighted regression.
control_architecture: DMP: a stable canonical dynamical system τṡ = -αs (phase variable) drives a transformation system τ ÿ = α(β(g - y) - τẏ) + f(s) producing trajectory y(t). Goal g is parameterizable post-learning, allowing trajectory adaptation to new targets. Compositional: multiple DMPs can be sequenced or superposed.
creator: Auke Jan Ijspeert, Jun Nakanishi, Stefan Schaal; USC + ATR Computational Neuroscience Laboratories
disclosure_citation: Ijspeert, Auke Jan, Nakanishi, Jun, Schaal, Stefan. 'Movement imitation with nonlinear dynamical systems in humanoid robots.' IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), Washington DC, May 2002: 1398-1403. Foundational consolidation: Ijspeert, A.J., Nakanishi, J., Hoffmann, H., Pastor, P., Schaal, S. 'Dynamical movement primitives: Learning attractor models for motor behaviors.' Neural Computation 25(2): 328-373, February 2013.
prior_art_notes: DMPs are the canonical academic disclosure of stability-guaranteed learnable motor primitives for humanoid robotics. Anticipates: (1) one-shot trajectory-from-demonstration learning with stability guarantees — directly relevant to claims on humanoid skill libraries built from human demonstration (a foundational pattern in every commercial humanoid program); (2) goal-parameterizable motor primitives — relevant to claims on adaptable humanoid skills; (3) compositional skill chaining — relevant to claims on humanoid behavior trees built from learned primitives. Heavily cited (>3000 citations across the series); the 2013 Neural Computation paper is the canonical reference. Modern humanoid skill-library patents face this 24-year-deep 102 anchor.

actuator_details: **The surgical procedure that enables intuitive multi-DOF prosthetic-arm control**. After upper-limb amputation, severed motor nerves are surgically re-routed to spare chest / back muscles. When the patient thinks 'open hand', the corresponding chest muscle contracts; surface-EMG electrodes pick up the signal and drive the prosthetic. Result: intuitive multi-DOF control without joystick / switch input. Without TMR, myoelectric prostheses are limited to 1-2 DoF (open/close, rotate). With TMR + pattern-recognition (Coapt 2013 commercial license), full multi-DoF anthropomorphic-hand control becomes feasible.

First clinical case 2002 at Rehabilitation Institute of Chicago (RIC; now Shirley Ryan AbilityLab). actuator_details: **Variable Stiffness Actuator (VSA)**: a serial-elastic actuator where the stiffness itself is mechanically adjustable in real time. Two motors per joint: one sets joint position, the other sets joint stiffness. Enables **soft-when-needed, stiff-when-needed** behavior — soft for safe collaboration, stiff for precision manipulation. The architectural cousin of the Pratt-Williamson SEA (corpus entry `pratt-williamson-sea`, 1995, fixed compliance) — VSAs add the variable-stiffness dimension.
control_architecture: Two-motor co-control: position-motor + stiffness-motor. The stiffness controller sets the spring's pretension or geometry.

actuator_details: **Capture Point theory of humanoid balance**: defines the **point on the ground where the robot must step to come to a complete stop**, given current center-of-mass position + velocity. Direct engineering anchor of modern humanoid balance controllers, used in: Boston Dynamics Atlas, IHMC's NASA Valkyrie + Atlas-running controllers, Honda P-series stabilization.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, originally demonstrated on taxi-driver route-prediction (>100k GPS trajectories); extended to manipulator and locomotion settings in subsequent work. prior_art_notes: Ziebart MaxEnt IRL is the canonical disambiguation of Abbeel-Ng IRL: choose the maximum-entropy reward consistent with feature expectations, yielding a unique log-linear policy. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on humanoid imitation that handles imperfect/noisy demonstrations — MaxEnt IRL is the foundational principled handling; (2) claims on reward learning where the policy is stochastic over trajectories — the log-linear distribution P(τ) ∝ exp(wᵀφ(τ)) is the explicit form; (3) claims on energy-based / score-based reward models for robotic learning — MaxEnt IRL anticipates the energy-based view embraced by modern guided-cost-learning (Finn et al. 2016) and adversarial IRL. >4000 citations; AAAI proceedings open access. Lineage to Finn-Levine GCL, Fu et al. AIRL, modern preference-tuning. Modern humanoid IRL filings face this 18-year-deep anchor.

actuator_details: Single-DOF universal gripper: balloon filled with granular material (coffee grounds, etc.) attached to a vacuum line. Pressing into an object deforms the granular medium around the object's shape; vacuum applied to the balloon jams the granular medium into a rigid shape, capturing the object.
control_architecture: binary state: relaxed (granular flow allowed) vs. jammed (granular medium rigid). Vacuum applied via single solenoid valve.

prior_art_notes: The Cornell jamming gripper introduces granular-jamming as a fundamental new class of robotic gripper. actuator_details: Variable-impedance anthropomorphic hand-arm system. Hand: 19-DoF five-fingered anthropomorphic hand ('Awiwi') driven by 38 tendons via 38 brushless DC motors located in the forearm. Each finger joint is antagonistically driven by tendon pairs, with mechanically programmable nonlinear elastic elements that implement variable joint stiffness analogous to human muscle co-contraction. Arm: 7-DoF arm with variable-stiffness joints (FSJ — Floating Spring Joint) using parallel elastic elements. Total system has 52 motors. Designed to survive collisions at human-like speeds via mechanical energy absorption rather than software safety.
control_architecture: Impedance control with mechanically programmable variable stiffness; antagonistic-tendon joint-level stiffness regulation in hardware (not just software). Uses DLR's joint-torque-impedance framework descending from Albu-Schäffer's lightweight-arm work. Demonstrated robustness to impact disturbances (hammer-strike experiments) without controller intervention because mechanical compliance absorbs the energy.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, demonstrated on simulated humanoid characters performing locomotion, climbing, manipulation, and acrobatic motions. CIO formulates motion synthesis as a single trajectory optimization problem in which contact existence and contact forces are continuous decision variables (rather than combinatorial mode switches). A complementarity-style regularization enforces contact constraints without requiring pre-specified contact schedules. Solved with an SQP-class nonlinear optimizer.
aliases: Discovery of Complex Behaviors through Contact-Invariant Optimization
control_architecture: Trajectory optimization with continuous-variable contact representation. The optimizer discovers when and where to place contacts (hand placement, foothold selection, manipulation grasps) as part of the same optimization that solves for joint torques and trajectories. Eliminates the manual design of contact sequences that hampered earlier trajectory optimization for humanoids.

disclosure_citation: Mordatch, Igor; Todorov, Emanuel; Popović, Zoran. 'Discovery of Complex Behaviors through Contact-Invariant Optimization.' 'Animating Human Lower Limbs Using Contact-Invariant Optimization.' ACM TOG (SIGGRAPH Asia 2013).

SIGGRAPH 2012 paper has >1000 citations and is foundational in both robotics and computer animation. Modern contact-implicit humanoid trajectory optimization IP faces this 14-year-deep academic anchor.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, demonstrated on simulated MuJoCo humanoid (28-DoF), swimmer, and cheetah models. Iterative Linear Quadratic Gaussian (iLQG) — a differential-dynamic-programming-class trajectory optimizer that linearizes the dynamics about a nominal trajectory and solves a sequence of LQG subproblems with regularization. Receding-horizon online application enables real-time MPC at >100 Hz on 28-DoF humanoid models. The 2012 paper introduces the regularization scheme and line search that made iLQG run online.

canonical_name: Tassa iLQG / Synthesis and Stabilization of Complex Behaviors
control_architecture: Online receding-horizon trajectory optimization (model-predictive control) via iLQG. Computes locally optimal feedback policies in addition to feedforward trajectories — i.e., the algorithm produces both u(t) and a time-varying gain K(t), giving stabilizing closed-loop control. Demonstrated humanoid getup, walking, and recovery from disturbances in MuJoCo simulation.

'Receding Horizon Differential Dynamic Programming.' NeurIPS 2007. Foundational underlying method: Li, W. and Todorov, E. prior_art_notes: Tassa-Erez-Todorov 2012 IROS is the canonical academic disclosure of online iLQG-based model-predictive control for high-DoF humanoid systems. Anticipates with full mathematical specificity: (1) online receding-horizon trajectory optimization for 28-DoF humanoid models at real-time rates — directly relevant to claims on humanoid MPC IP (Boston Dynamics, Apptronik, Figure, Tesla all employ trajectory-optimization-class controllers); (2) the regularization-and-line-search scheme that enabled iLQG to run online with stable convergence — anticipates implementation-detail patents on regularized DDP/iLQG humanoid controllers; (3) jointly synthesizing feedforward trajectories AND time-varying feedback gains — relevant to claims on closed-loop humanoid trajectory IP. Foundational lineage: Li-Todorov ICINCO 2004 (iLQR primitive); Jacobson-Mayne 1970 (DDP); Bellman 1957 (dynamic programming). Direct downstream: every major modern humanoid MPC stack.

Integrates OMPL planners (RRT, RRT*, PRM, etc.), kinematic constraint satisfaction, collision checking (FCL), trajectory smoothing. **Used by every academic + industrial robot integrating with ROS**. BSD-3 open-source. The de facto motion-planning library for the field 2013-2025.

actuator_details: Framework demonstrated on Sarcos Slave Arm, ATRIAS, ASIMO-class simulators, Barrett WAM. Discrete and rhythmic DMPs disclosed in canonical second-order ODE form: τż = αz(βz(g − y) − z) + f(x), with phase variable x and forcing term f(x) parameterized by Gaussian basis weights learned from demonstration.
control_architecture: dynamical-system attractor model with phase-coupled forcing term; supports discrete (point-attractor) and rhythmic (limit-cycle) primitives, online goal modulation, and obstacle-avoidance via coupling terms. Provably stable convergence; closed-form per-DOF formulation.

disclosure_citation: Ijspeert, Auke Jan, Nakanishi, Jun, Hoffmann, Heiko, Pastor, Peter, Schaal, Stefan. 'Dynamical Movement Primitives: Learning Attractor Models for Motor Behaviors.' International Symposium on Robotics Research (ISRR) 2003; Schaal, Mohajerian, Ijspeert. 'Dynamics systems vs. optimal control — a unifying view.' Progress in Brain Research 165: 425-445, 2007.
prior_art_notes: Ijspeert-Schaal DMPs are the canonical academic disclosure of learnable, stable, parameterized motor primitives for robotic motion generation. The 2013 Neural Computation paper consolidates the formal framework; the 2007 Progress in Brain Research extension and the 2002-2003 Schaal/Ijspeert papers establish lineage. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on demonstration-learned humanoid motion primitives with online goal modulation — DMPs disclose the closed-form ODE structure used in essentially every humanoid skill-library paper since 2007; (2) claims on rhythmic locomotion primitives with phase coupling — directly anticipates pattern-generator humanoid IP; (3) claims on obstacle-avoiding modulated motion primitives — the coupling-term extension is explicit in the 2013 paper. >5000 citations; broadly available through open Neural Computation archives. Modern humanoid skill-primitive IP filings face this lineage at 13-23 years' depth.

actuator_details: Six-legged sprawl-tuned crawling robot (~75 g class). Single brushless DC motor drives a four-bar mechanism that produces alternating tripod leg motion. **Sprawl angle is mechanically tunable** between flat (legs splayed wide) and tall (legs pulled in) configurations to adapt to different terrains and obstacle types. PCB-process-fabricated linkage frames; passive compliance via flexible polymer.
control_architecture: Open-loop alternating-tripod gait; sprawl angle is mechanically set per terrain. Pre-programmed mission patterns; no real-time adaptation.

actuator_details: Three-finger underactuated tendon-driven hand. Each finger: two phalanges with passive compliant joints and a single tendon for flexion + a spring antagonist for extension. Whole hand: three motors (one per finger) plus optional palm-rotation degree of freedom. Designed for inherent grasp robustness via underactuation and compliant adaptation. ReFlex SF (Sensorized Finger) variant adds tactile fingertip sensors via the TakkTile MEMS array technology.
control_architecture: Single-DoF-per-finger tendon position or torque control; passive compliance handles object shape variation. Yale OpenHand Project provides multiple parametric hand variants (Model M, Model O, Model T42) all sharing the underactuated-tendon paradigm. Open-source ROS drivers for ReFlex SF.

actuator_details: Algorithmic and control disclosure on the original Boston Dynamics Atlas hydraulic humanoid (DRC-era; 28 hydraulically actuated DoF, ~150 kg). Papers describe whole-body QP-based inverse-dynamics control, footstep-region MIP planning (Deits-Tedrake 2014), iterative SQP trajectory optimization, contact-aware Kalman-filter state estimation, and the IRIS region-of-attraction footstep planner. Publications cover Atlas's entire controller stack as deployed at the DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals (June 2015).
canonical_name: Atlas academic publications (Kuindersma et al., DRC era)
control_architecture: Whole-body inverse-dynamics QP control: at every control step solve a quadratic program for joint torques minimizing tracking error subject to contact constraints, friction cones, and torque limits. Footstep planning via mixed-integer convex optimization over the IRIS regions decomposition of free space. Trajectory optimization via direct transcription with SQP. Contact-aware EKF state estimation. The Kuindersma 2016 AURO paper provides the consolidated end-to-end controller architecture.
creator: Scott Kuindersma, Russ Tedrake, Robin Deits, Maurice Fallon, Andrés Valenzuela, Hongkai Dai, Frank Permenter, Twan Koolen, Pat Marion; MIT CSAIL Robot Locomotion Group (DRC Atlas team)

Anticipates with element-by-element specificity: (1) whole-body QP-based inverse-dynamics control on a hydraulically-actuated humanoid platform — directly relevant to commercial claims on QP-based humanoid IP (every modern humanoid runs a derivative); (2) the IRIS-regions mixed-integer convex footstep planner — relevant to claims on footstep-planning humanoid IP; (3) iterative SQP trajectory optimization with contact schedule — anticipates claims overlapping Crocoddyl (mastalli-crocoddyl-2020) and DDP approaches; (4) the consolidated end-to-end stack documentation in AURO 2016 — the most complete public disclosure of a working DRC-class humanoid control architecture. actuator_details: Willow Garage PR2 dual-arm humanoid platform (BRETT in Berkeley lab branding). Each arm 7-DoF compliant; 3-finger gripper. End-to-end CNN policy mapping 240×240 RGB to 7-DoF torques learned via guided policy search (GPS): trajectory-optimization-supervised neural-network distillation.
canonical_name: Levine Guided Policy Search end-to-end manipulation on PR2/BRETT
control_architecture: Guided Policy Search: alternates between (a) trajectory optimization under known dynamics from initial states, producing reference trajectories; and (b) supervised neural-network training to imitate the trajectory-optimizer. Final policy is a convolutional network mapping camera pixels directly to torques. Multi-task generalization across coat-hanger, plastic-bottle, hammer, screw insertion.

disclosure_citation: Levine, Sergey, Finn, Chelsea, Darrell, Trevor, Abbeel, Pieter. 'End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies.' 'Learning Contact-Rich Manipulation Skills with Guided Policy Search.' ICRA 2015.

Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on end-to-end neural-network policies mapping camera observations directly to humanoid actuator commands — Levine's CNN architecture, training pipeline, and on-robot evaluation are explicitly disclosed; (2) claims on trajectory-optimization-supervised distillation as a sample-efficient alternative to model-free RL on physical humanoids — GPS is the headline contribution; (3) claims on multi-task generalization of a single visuomotor network across contact-rich manipulation tasks (coat-hanger, plastic-bottle, hammer, screw insertion). >3500 citations; JMLR open access; arXiv preprint 2015. The lineage runs directly forward to RT-1, RT-2, OpenVLA, and modern humanoid VLA systems. Modern humanoid end-to-end visuomotor IP filings face this 11-year-deep anchor with full architecture disclosure.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure. Imitation learning formulated as occupancy-measure matching: a discriminator network (GAN-like) learns to distinguish expert state-action pairs from policy state-action pairs, while the policy is trained via TRPO/PPO with the discriminator's negative log-probability as reward.
control_architecture: GAN-style two-network training: (1) discriminator D(s,a) → [0,1] trained to maximize log D(s,a)_expert + log(1 - D(s,a)_policy); (2) policy π(a|s) trained via policy gradient with reward r(s,a) = -log(1 - D(s,a)). Bypasses inverse-RL's expensive cost-function recovery.

disclosure_citation: Ho, Jonathan and Ermon, Stefano. 'Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning.' arXiv:1606.03476, June 10, 2016. NeurIPS 2016: 4565-4573.

notable_capabilities: demonstrated on humanoid walker MuJoCo benchmark
prior_art_notes: GAIL is the foundational academic disclosure of GAN-style adversarial imitation learning, providing a sample-efficient alternative to inverse-RL for policy learning from demonstration. Anticipates: (1) the discriminator-as-reward-source paradigm for imitation — directly relevant to claims on humanoid policies trained via adversarial-loss imitation (a common ingredient in modern legged-robot RL pipelines); (2) the elimination of cost-function recovery as a separate step — relevant to claims on end-to-end imitation pipelines for humanoids; (3) the demonstrated MuJoCo Humanoid benchmark transfer — relevant to humanoid-RL patent claims. Heavily cited (>4000 citations). Open-source reference implementation. Modern humanoid adversarial-imitation-learning patent claims face this 10-year-deep anchor.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure for goal-conditioned RL. Demonstrated on Fetch and Shadow Hand simulation environments. The HER mechanism: relabel failed trajectories with achieved goals as the desired goals, providing dense reward signal even when the original goal was missed.

actuator_details: **Foundational motion-capture-imitation reinforcement learning** for physics-based character animation. actuator_details: Augmented two-synergy underactuated anthropomorphic hand: 19 internal DoFs driven by TWO motors (vs. one in the original SoftHand). Each motor drives an independent tendon routed through a distinct postural synergy derived from PCA on human grasping kinematics. The two synergies span a richer subspace of grasp+manipulation than the single-synergy predecessor — the second synergy enables abduction/adduction patterns and limited in-hand manipulation. Compliant elastic-return joints throughout; passive shape adaptation.
control_architecture: Two-DoF tendon position control along the two principal grasping synergies; supports in-hand re-grasping by trajectories within the augmented synergy subspace. Compliant joints handle object shape variation passively, eliminating the need for explicit perception-driven grasp planning.
creator: Cosimo Della Santina, Cristina Piazza, Giorgio Grioli, Manuel G. Catalano, Antonio Bicchi; Centro 'E. Piaggio', Università di Pisa, and Italian Institute of Technology (IIT)
disclosure_citation: Della Santina, Cosimo; Piazza, Cristina; Grioli, Giorgio; Catalano, Manuel G.; Bicchi, Antonio. 'Toward Dexterous Manipulation With Augmented Adaptive Synergies: The Pisa/IIT SoftHand 2.' IEEE Transactions on Robotics, Volume 34, Issue 5, October 2018, pp. 1141-1156. DOI: 10.1109/TRO.2018.2830407. First public disclosure as a conference work in earlier 2017 venues; the consolidated T-RO paper is the canonical reference.
notable_capabilities: 19-DoF anthropomorphic hand with only 2 motors via augmented synergies
in-hand manipulation enabled by the second synergy direction
passive shape adaptation via compliant elastic returns
prior_art_notes: Pisa-IIT SoftHand 2 (Della Santina et al. T-RO 2018) is the canonical academic disclosure of multi-synergy augmented underactuated anthropomorphic hands, extending the 2014 SoftHand from one synergy to two. Anticipates with element-by-element specificity: (1) the augmented multi-synergy actuation pattern that enables 19-DoF hand operation with 2 motors and provides in-hand manipulation capability — directly relevant to claims on low-motor-count dexterous humanoid hand IP (Tesla Optimus claimed motor-counts in the 11-22 range, Figure-02 hand counts similar; the SoftHand 2 paradigm anticipates the underactuation-with-manipulation-capability angle of those claims); (2) the formal extension of synergy theory from grasping (one synergy) to grasping-plus-manipulation (two synergies) — relevant to claims on synergy-based humanoid manipulation IP; (3) compliant passive shape adaptation eliminating perception-driven grasp planning — relevant to claims on perception-light humanoid grasping IP. Heavily cited (>200); consolidates Bicchi-group underactuation lineage from the 1990s. Modern multi-synergy underactuated humanoid hand IP filings face this 8-year-deep academic anchor.
sensing: motor positions (2), cable tensions, optional fingertip force sensors
sources: Della Santina, C. et al. 'Toward Dexterous Manipulation With Augmented Adaptive Synergies: The Pisa/IIT SoftHand 2.' IEEE T-RO 34(5): 1141-1156, October 2018. DOI: 10.1109/TRO.2018.2830407.

actuator_details: **The foundational modern diffusion-models paper**. Iterative noise-removal generative process: noise images progressively, then train a model to reverse the process. The architectural anchor of: Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 2/3, Midjourney, Sora, **and Diffusion Policy** (corpus entry diffusion-policy) + every diffusion-based VLA (RDT-1B round-13, π₀ round-12, DP3 round-17). Antecedent Sohl-Dickstein 2015 introduced diffusion in ML; Ho 2020 made it practical.

notable_capabilities: the architectural anchor of every diffusion-based VLA
prior_art_notes: DDPM (Ho et al. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on diffusion-based action generation. Closes a major foundational citation chain.

actuator_details: **Perseverance: sample-caching Curiosity successor. Ingenuity: FIRST POWERED CONTROLLED FLIGHT OFF EARTH**. The first aerial vehicle on another planet — landmark Wright-brothers-class achievement.

actuator_details: Architecture: jointly trains an image encoder and a text encoder to embed images and text descriptions into a shared vector space using contrastive loss over 400M (image, text) pairs scraped from the web. Resulting embeddings enable zero-shot classification, image retrieval, image-text alignment for downstream tasks.
control_architecture: visual-language alignment substrate; CLIP embeddings are used as a frozen perception backbone in many VLA humanoid policies (PaLM-E, Open X-Embodiment, RT-2 all use CLIP-class encoders or directly fine-tuned CLIP)
creator: Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim, Chris Hallacy, Aditya Ramesh, et al.; OpenAI
disclosure_citation: Radford, Alec; Kim, Jong Wook; Hallacy, Chris; Ramesh, Aditya; Goh, Gabriel; Agarwal, Sandhini; Sastry, Girish; Askell, Amanda; Mishkin, Pamela; Clark, Jack; Krueger, Gretchen; Sutskever, Ilya. 'Learning transferable visual models from natural language supervision'. arXiv:2103.00020, February 26, 2021. Published ICML 2021.
prior_art_notes: CLIP 2021 is the foundational academic disclosure of contrastive vision-language pretraining at internet scale. Anticipates: (1) the use of contrastive image-text pretraining as a frozen perception backbone for humanoid VLA policies — directly relevant to modern VLA humanoid claims (RT-2, Open X-Embodiment, OpenVLA, PaLM-E, π-zero all build on CLIP-class architectures); (2) zero-shot perception via natural-language descriptions of target objects — relevant to claims on language-conditioned humanoid manipulation; (3) the architecture of training visual encoders on uncurated web data — relevant to data-scaling claims. Modern VLA humanoid IP all face this 5-year academic anchor.
sources: Radford, A. et al. 'Learning transferable visual models from natural language supervision'. arXiv:2103.00020, ICML 2021.

actuator_details: **First soft robot operating freely at hadal depth (10,900 m)**. 22 cm soft-elastomer body inspired by hadal snailfish. Distributed silicone-elastomer pressure-tolerant electronics embedded in the soft body (no rigid pressure housings). Flapping-fin propulsion + dielectric-elastomer actuators. Free-swimming demonstration in Mariana Trench (10,900 m) + South China Sea (3,224 m). Landmark hadal soft-robotics result. Nature March 2021 publication.
control_architecture: Onboard control; pressure-tolerant distributed electronics in silicone matrix.
creator: Beihang University + Zhejiang University + Westlake University (China); Guorui Li et al.

notable_capabilities: first soft robot operating freely at hadal depth (2021)
Mariana Trench 10,900 m + South China Sea 3,224 m demonstrations
prior_art_notes: Beihang hadal soft robot (Nature March 2021) is the first soft robot operating freely at hadal depth (10,900 m Mariana Trench). 4-year-deep academic-publication prior art. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid or aquatic-robot claim deriving from pressure-tolerant soft robotics or hadal-zone soft-elastomer vehicles.
sources: Li, G. et al. Nature 591:66-71, March 2021.

actuator_details: Visual-inertial SLAM library. ORB feature extraction + bag-of-words place recognition + bundle adjustment over keyframes. Supports monocular, stereo, RGB-D, and visual-inertial sensor configurations. Multi-map operation with map-merging. Real-time on commodity CPU.
control_architecture: Provides SLAM substrate for any robotic platform with a camera. C++ library; ROS 1/2 integration.

IEEE Transactions on Robotics 37(6) December 2021, pp. 1874-1890. arXiv:2007.11898. GPLv3 source: github.com/UZ-SLAMLab/ORB_SLAM3. University of Zaragoza.

deployed in countless academic + commercial robotic systems
prior_art_notes: ORB-SLAM3 is the canonical academic visual-inertial SLAM library and 5-year-deep open-source baseline. Heavily-cited (>3000 citations). Anticipates: (1) monocular/stereo/RGB-D + IMU fusion in a unified factor-graph framework, (2) multi-map operation across sessions for long-term autonomy, (3) bag-of-words place recognition for loop closure. Establishes the geometric-only SLAM baseline that semantic/open-vocab SLAM systems (including RADIO-ViPE, round-10 entry) extend. Any humanoid platform claim on visual-inertial SLAM faces this lineage.

actuator_details: **Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP)** — combines DeepMimic-style motion-capture imitation with **GAN-style discriminator** trained to distinguish reference-motion-style from policy-generated motion. Replaces DeepMimic's clip-by-clip imitation with **latent-space style imitation** — the policy can produce task-specific motion that 'looks like' the reference style without exactly tracking any specific clip. Major architectural advance over DeepMimic: **distillation of motion style from unstructured motion-capture corpus** rather than clip-specific imitation.
control_architecture: GAN discriminator distilled from motion-capture corpus + task reward + RL policy. Latent style space.
creator: UC Berkeley; Xue Bin (Jason) Peng, Ze Ma, Pieter Abbeel, Sergey Levine, Angjoo Kanazawa
disclosure_citation: Peng, X. B., Ma, Z., Abbeel, P., Levine, S., Kanazawa, A. 'AMP: Adversarial Motion Priors for Stylized Physics-Based Character Control'. ACM Transactions on Graphics 40(4) 2021 (SIGGRAPH 2021). arXiv:2104.02180. UC Berkeley.
notable_capabilities: GAN-style motion-prior distillation from unstructured mocap corpus
the architectural anchor of subsequent AMP-derived humanoid RL papers
open-source via NVIDIA Isaac Gym + Berkeley repos
prior_art_notes: Adversarial Motion Priors (Peng et al. SIGGRAPH 2021) is the canonical extension of DeepMimic to GAN-style latent-space motion imitation. 4-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: GAN-distilled motion priors, latent-space mocap style imitation, task-conditioned style-aware humanoid RL. **The architectural ancestor of contemporary humanoid-from-mocap RL** including ASE (Peng et al. 2022), HumanPlus (Stanford 2024), ExBody (Stanford 2024), H1 / G1 humanoid policies (Unitree). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on 'humanoid moves like a human' style-aware locomotion.
sources: Peng, X. B. et al. ACM TOG 40(4) 2021; arXiv:2104.02180.

actuator_details: **Reframes reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling using a Transformer**. Given a target return-to-go + past state-action history, predict the next action. **The conceptual precursor of VLA**: cast policy learning as next-token-prediction with a Transformer backbone. Direct architectural ancestor of: RT-1 (action-as-token), GATO (DM multi-task agent), VLA architecture broadly.
control_architecture: Transformer that takes (return, state, action) sequences as input; predicts next action conditioned on return target.
creator: UC Berkeley + FAIR + Google Brain; Lili Chen, Kevin Lu, Pieter Abbeel, Igor Mordatch et al.
disclosure_citation: Chen, L., Lu, K., Rajeswaran, A., Lee, K., Grover, A., Laskin, M., Abbeel, P., Srinivas, A., Mordatch, I. 'Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling'. NeurIPS 2021. arXiv:2106.01345. UC Berkeley + Facebook AI Research + Google Brain.
