Transformer backbone applied to control sequences
prior_art_notes: Decision Transformer (Chen et al. NeurIPS 2021) is the foundational paper recasting RL as conditional sequence modeling. 4-year-deep public-domain prior art. **The conceptual precursor of VLA architecture** — every VLA in the corpus (RT-1, RT-2, OpenVLA, π₀, GR00T N1, Helix) implicitly applies this framing. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on Transformer-based control policies.

actuator_details: Successor to FSTAR adding **wall-climbing via thrust reversal**. Propellers can produce reversed thrust; combined with 4-wheel drive, the robot drives over steep slopes including walls. Penetrates 25 cm diameter pipes. Ground speed up to 4.5 m/s. The most architecturally extreme STAR-family member to date.
control_architecture: Mode-switching: ground / wall-climbing / pipe-traversal / flight, with shared actuator pool.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; David Zarrouk group
disclosure_citation: Zarrouk, D., et al. 'FCSTAR: Design and Analysis of a Hybrid Flying and Climbing Sprawl-Tuned Robot'. ResearchGate publication 353205537, July 2021. Ben-Gurion University. Builds on FSTAR with thrust-reversal wall-climbing capability.
notable_capabilities: STAR-family extension that further validates shared-actuator-pool design
notes: DRAFT: exact peer-reviewed venue should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: FCSTAR (Ben-Gurion Zarrouk lab, ~2021) is the most architecturally ambitious STAR-family member: 4 modes (ground, wall-climb, pipe, flight) on a single actuator pool. 4-year-deep open-academic prior art for: thrust-reversal wall-climbing, multi-mode-on-shared-actuator-pool reconfiguration, narrow-pipe traversal. Closes the STAR family lineage chain that begins at star-fearing-2013 and ends with dstar-zarrouk-2026 (decoupled FBEM, Jan 2026). The full 13-year-deep STAR family chain: STAR (Berkeley 2013) → RSTAR (Zarrouk 2019) → TSTAR → FSTAR → FCSTAR → AmphiSTAR → DSTAR.

actuator_details: GPU-parallelized physics simulator for robotic RL. End-to-end GPU pipeline: simulation, observation extraction, neural network inference, policy update — no CPU round-trip. Enables thousands of parallel environment instances on a single GPU. The substrate for ANYmal sim-to-real perceptive locomotion (Hwangbo 2019 → Lee 2020 → Miki 2022 lineage).

Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on GPU-parallelized RL training; particularly the thousands-of-parallel-envs scaling that commercial humanoid vendors cite as proprietary.

actuator_details: **Dexterous manipulation policy training from human videos** (rather than robot teleoperation). Pipeline: (1) extract human hand pose from in-the-wild videos via a hand-pose estimator, (2) retarget to a 30-DoF Adroit anthropomorphic hand, (3) train a manipulation policy via IL + RL refinement in SAPIEN. Demo tasks: pour, place, relocate, hammer use. Direct conceptual ancestor of NVIDIA GR00T N1's egocentric-video-pretraining approach.
control_architecture: IL from retargeted human poses + RL refinement; SAPIEN simulator backend.

the canonical academic ancestor of egocentric-video-trained humanoid policies

Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on 'we trained on YouTube videos' or 'egocentric-video-based policy pretraining'.

actuator_details: Hybrid bipedal-aerial robot. Two articulated legs each with 3 actuated DoF (hip, knee, ankle) for ground locomotion. Each leg also carries a propeller (so 4 propellers total: two per foot/ankle area) for aerial flight and balance assistance during walking. Brushless DC actuators throughout. Total mass ~2.5 kg. Designed to switch fluidly between bipedal walking and quadcopter-style flight, plus mixed modes (slacklining, skateboarding) where propellers provide balance authority while legs handle ground contact.
control_architecture: Hybrid bipedal-aerial nonlinear MPC. Onboard IMU and motion-capture localization for outdoor/indoor flight. Walking gaits stabilized via simultaneous use of leg actuation and propeller thrust — propellers provide ankle-torque-augmenting forces that ZMP-class bipeds cannot exploit. Demonstrated slackline traversal, skateboarding, stair descent.
creator: Kyunam Kim, Patrick Spieler, Alireza Ramezani, Soon-Jo Chung; Caltech Aerospace Robotics and Control Lab (Chung group), CAST (Center for Autonomous Systems and Technologies)
disclosure_citation: Kim, Kyunam; Spieler, Patrick; Lupu, Elena-Sorina; Ramezani, Alireza; Chung, Soon-Jo. 'A bipedal walking robot that can fly, slackline, and skateboard.' Science Robotics, Volume 6, Issue 59, October 6, 2021, eabf8136. DOI: 10.1126/scirobotics.abf8136. Caltech CAST press release October 6, 2021.
notable_capabilities: fluid switching between bipedal walking and quadcopter flight
balance-assist via propellers during walking (novel mechanism)
prior_art_notes: Caltech LEONARDO (Kim-Chung et al. Science Robotics 2021) is the canonical academic disclosure of bipedal-aerial hybrid morphology with simultaneous walking-and-thrust-balance-assist control. Anticipates with element-by-element specificity: (1) the hybrid-morphology bipedal-aerial platform with propellers integrated into the leg structure — directly relevant to claims on hybrid-locomotion humanoid IP, anticipating any future commercial humanoid that augments walking with thrust assistance; (2) simultaneous use of propeller thrust and leg actuation for balance during walking — relevant to claims on multi-modal balance authority for humanoid platforms (separate from ZMP-only or angular-momentum-only approaches); (3) the demonstration on extreme tasks (slackline traversal, skateboarding) that exceed the capability set of pure bipedal robots — relevant to claims on extreme-environment humanoid mobility IP. Science Robotics paper provides full design and control disclosure. Modern hybrid-locomotion humanoid IP faces this 5-year-deep academic anchor.
sensing: IMU, motion capture (in lab); onboard cameras in later variants
sources: Kim, K. et al. 'A bipedal walking robot that can fly, slackline, and skateboard.' Science Robotics 6(59), eabf8136, October 2021. DOI: 10.1126/scirobotics.abf8136.
Caltech CAST press release: 'Meet LEO, the Bipedal Robot That Can Skateboard and Fly,' October 6, 2021.

actuator_details: Quasi-direct-drive (QDD) actuators throughout — direct lineage from the Mini Cheetah actuator design (low-gear-ratio, high-torque-density brushless motors with custom motor controllers). 18 actuated DoF: 5 per leg, 4 per arm, plus a torso. Light-weight design (~24 kg) compared to hydraulic-class humanoids. Backdrivable joints enable proprioceptive torque sensing without dedicated torque sensors.
control_architecture: Convex MPC with explicit actuator-dynamics model (motor inertia, torque limits, current limits) integrated into the optimization. Centroidal-momentum-based reduced-order model for online MPC. Capable of acrobatic behaviors (jumps, flips) via offline trajectory optimization combined with online tracking.
creator: Matthew Chignoli, Donghyun Kim, Elijah Stanger-Jones, Sangbae Kim; MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab
disclosure_citation: Chignoli, Matthew; Kim, Donghyun; Stanger-Jones, Elijah; Kim, Sangbae. 'The MIT Humanoid Robot: Design, Motion Planning, and Control For Acrobatic Behaviors.' IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids 2020, virtual; presented November 2021), pp. 1-8. arXiv:2104.09025, April 2021.
end_effector: point feet (no manipulation in baseline platform)
notable_capabilities: QDD actuator topology applied to humanoid biped
actuator-dynamics-aware MPC for whole-body humanoid control
acrobatic capabilities (jumps, flips) via TO + MPC
prior_art_notes: The MIT Humanoid (Chignoli-Kim et al. Humanoids 2020/arXiv 2021) is the canonical academic disclosure of dynamic whole-body humanoid locomotion using a quasi-direct-drive actuator topology with explicit actuator-dynamics-aware MPC, from the Sangbae Kim group (MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab) that previously produced Mini Cheetah and Cheetah 3. Anticipates with element-by-element specificity: (1) QDD actuator topology extended from quadruped (Mini Cheetah, 2019) to humanoid biped — directly relevant to commercial claims on QDD humanoid IP (Berkeley Humanoid, Unitree H1/G1, Booster T1, much of the 2024-2026 humanoid wave employs QDD); (2) explicit actuator-dynamics-model integration into humanoid MPC (motor inertia, torque limits, current limits enter the OCP directly) — anticipates commercial claims on actuator-aware humanoid control; (3) acrobatic-capable lightweight (~24 kg) electric humanoid as a research platform — anticipates the lightweight-humanoid commercial form factor. The Sangbae Kim lineage (Cheetah 1/2/3 → Mini Cheetah → MIT Humanoid) is one of the deepest legged-robot academic chains and the MIT Humanoid arXiv preprint provides full design documentation. Modern QDD-humanoid IP filings face this 5-year-deep academic anchor.

actuator_details: **Magnetic-based tactile skin**. A thin elastomeric skin embeds randomly-oriented magnetic particles; an underlying array of magnetometers detects skin deformation via local magnetic-field changes. **Replaceable + low-cost (~$5 per skin)**: when the skin wears out, peel and replace; the sensor electronics underneath are reused. Distinct from vision-based tactile (DIGIT, GelSight) by sensing modality.
control_architecture: Provides magnetic-deformation signal stream; learned-network mapping to force / contact-position estimates.
creator: Carnegie Mellon University + Meta AI Research; Bhirangi, Hellebrekers, Majidi, Gupta
disclosure_citation: Bhirangi, R., Hellebrekers, T., Majidi, C., Gupta, A. 'ReSkin: versatile, replaceable, lasting tactile skins'. CoRL 2021. arXiv:2111.00071, November 2021. Carnegie Mellon University + Meta AI Research.
end_effector: magnetic-tactile skin (mountable on any gripper / hand surface)
prior_art_notes: ReSkin is the canonical magnetic-based tactile-skin academic anchor (Bhirangi et al. CoRL 2021). 4-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: magnetic-particle-embedded elastomeric tactile skin, replaceable-skin (peel-and-replace) tactile-sensor architecture, low-cost (<$10/skin) tactile-sensor designs. Distinct from DIGIT/GelSight (vision-based) by sensing modality — complementary prior art. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on magnetic-based tactile skin or replaceable-tactile-skin architecture.
sensing: magnetometer array under elastomeric magnetic-particle skin

actuator_details: **Self-supervised vision pretraining via masked-patch reconstruction**. Mask 75% of an image's patches; train the decoder to reconstruct missing pixels from visible ones. Provides excellent visual features for downstream tasks without labeled data. **The pretraining method of VC-1 (round-29) and many embodied AI vision encoders**.
control_architecture: N/A — pretraining method.

notable_capabilities: the pretraining method of VC-1 + many embodied AI vision encoders
prior_art_notes: MAE (He et al. CVPR 2022) is the canonical self-supervised masked-patch-reconstruction vision pretraining method. 4-year-deep public-domain prior art. **The pretraining method of VC-1** (round-29 entry) and many embodied AI vision encoders. Together with DINOv2 (round-13), establishes the self-supervised vision-pretraining academic substrate.

actuator_details: End-to-end differentiable visual SLAM. Dense bundle adjustment over all pixels (vs. ORB-SLAM's sparse keypoint approach). Recurrent iterative optical-flow updates produce dense correspondences and depth. GPU-accelerated. Significantly more robust to texture-poor scenes and dynamic content than ORB-SLAM3.
control_architecture: Visual SLAM substrate. PyTorch implementation; supports monocular/stereo/RGB-D inputs.
creator: Princeton Vision and Learning Lab; Zachary Teed, Jia Deng
disclosure_citation: Teed, Z., Deng, J. 'DROID-SLAM: Deep Visual SLAM for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras'. NeurIPS 2021. arXiv:2108.10869. BSD-3-Clause source: github.com/princeton-vl/DROID-SLAM. Princeton Vision and Learning Lab.
notable_capabilities: robust to texture-poor and dynamic scenes
the foundation for ViPE and downstream semantic SLAM systems
prior_art_notes: DROID-SLAM is the canonical dense differentiable-visual-SLAM academic system (NeurIPS 2021, BSD-3 open source). 4-year-deep prior art anticipating any humanoid claim on dense / differentiable / foundation-model-grounded visual SLAM. Immediate ancestor of ViPE (Princeton 2024-2025) and RADIO-ViPE (ITMO 2026 — round-10 entry). Together with ORB-SLAM3, establishes the academic SLAM baseline against which all modern humanoid perception claims must be evaluated.
sources: Predecessor: RAFT (Teed/Deng ECCV 2020) for optical flow.

actuator_details: **Long-horizon language-conditioned manipulation benchmark**. Four interactive simulated environments with sliding doors, drawers, buttons, switches, colored blocks. **~24 hours of teleoperated unstructured 'play' data + 20K language directives + ~2.4M interaction steps + 389 unique natural-language instructions across 34 tasks**. Distinguished from RLBench/robomimic by language-conditioning + long-horizon focus.
control_architecture: Provides task suite + dataset + standard baselines for language-conditioned IL. Open-source.
creator: University of Freiburg AIS Lab; Oier Mees, Lukas Hermann, Wolfram Burgard
disclosure_citation: Mees, O., Hermann, L., Rosete-Beas, E., Burgard, W. 'CALVIN: A Benchmark for Language-Conditioned Policy Learning for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation Tasks'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 7(3) 2022. arXiv:2112.03227. University of Freiburg.
prior_art_notes: CALVIN is the canonical long-horizon language-conditioned manipulation benchmark (Mees + Burgard Freiburg, RA-L 2022). 4-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: language-conditioned robot manipulation benchmark, teleoperated 'play data' as training distribution, hour-scale unstructured play datasets for language grounding. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on language-conditioned manipulation training data + benchmarks. Together with LIBERO (round-17), RoboCasa (round-16), robomimic (round-16), establishes the language-conditioned-VLA evaluation substrate.
sources: Mees et al. arXiv:2112.03227 IEEE RA-L 2022.

actuator_details: **Foundational language-conditioned manipulation policy at Google Everyday Robots scale**. Trained on 25,877 demonstrations from 100 manipulation tasks across 7 distinct mobile-manipulator robots. **Architecture: ResNet visual encoder + language embedding (universal sentence encoder) + action policy**. Demonstrates zero-shot task generalization. Direct architectural ancestor of RT-1 (corpus entry rt-1) which extended BC-Z's framework with Transformer architecture.
control_architecture: ResNet + USE language embedding + action policy. Foundational language-conditioned IL framework.
creator: Google Research + Stanford + Everyday Robots; Eric Jang, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn et al.
disclosure_citation: Jang, E., Irpan, A., Khansari, M., Kappler, D., Ebert, F., Lynch, C., Levine, S., Finn, C. 'BC-Z: Zero-Shot Task Generalization with Robotic Imitation Learning'. CoRL 2021. arXiv:2202.02005. Google Research + Stanford + Everyday Robots.
notable_capabilities: first language-conditioned manipulation policy at Google scale
the architectural ancestor of RT-1 + the entire RT-X lineage
prior_art_notes: BC-Z (Jang et al. CoRL 2021) is the foundational language-conditioned manipulation policy paper at Google scale. 4-year-deep public-domain prior art. **Direct architectural ancestor of RT-1** (corpus entry) which transformerized BC-Z's framework. Established the 'large-scale demonstrations + language conditioning' pattern that the entire RT-X lineage descends from. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid VLA claim on 'large-scale teleop + language conditioning'.

actuator_details: **Perceptive RL locomotion for quadrupeds** — extends Hwangbo's ANYmal sim-to-real (corpus entry hwangbo-anymal-sim2real, 2019, blind locomotion) by integrating **exteroceptive vision** (depth from elevation maps) with proprioception. Achieves robust locomotion in challenging unstructured terrains (snow, dense vegetation, rubble, slippery surfaces). The current SOTA academic quadruped RL — directly cited by every modern quadruped RL paper. **Two-stage privileged-teacher / proprioception-+-exteroception-student distillation**.
control_architecture: Two-stage student-teacher distillation: privileged teacher trained with full state info → student trained with proprioception + depth-elevation-map only. Robust to perception failures via consistent recurrent state.
creator: ETH Zürich RSL + Intel Labs; Takahiro Miki, Joonho Lee, Jemin Hwangbo, Lorenz Wellhausen, Vladlen Koltun, Marco Hutter
disclosure_citation: Miki, T., Lee, J., Hwangbo, J., Wellhausen, L., Koltun, V., Hutter, M. 'Learning Robust Perceptive Locomotion for Quadrupedal Robots in the Wild'. Science Robotics 7(62) 2022. ETH Zürich Robotic Systems Lab + Intel Labs.
notable_capabilities: robust quadruped locomotion in snow, dense vegetation, rubble, slippery surfaces
the current SOTA academic quadruped RL
the architectural anchor of every subsequent quadruped RL paper 2022-2025
prior_art_notes: The Miki et al. Science Robotics 2022 perceptive-ANYmal paper is the canonical academic perceptive-quadruped-RL work. 3-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: privileged-teacher / proprioception+exteroception-student two-stage distillation, robust unstructured-terrain RL locomotion, depth-elevation-map perceptive locomotion. Direct successor to Hwangbo ANYmal sim-to-real (corpus entry, 2019). **The architectural ancestor of every modern quadruped + humanoid RL locomotion paper** including Berkeley Humanoid, ToddlerBot, Atlas Electric (round-18). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on perceptive-RL locomotion or unstructured-terrain RL training.

actuator_details: **Reusable adversarial skill embeddings for physics-based characters**. Successor to AMP (round-21 entry, SIGGRAPH 2021). Trains a **latent skill space** via GAN-style adversarial training on motion-capture data; downstream task policies sample from this latent space. Enables **task-conditioned skill reuse** across many physics-based-character tasks. Direct architectural ancestor of HumanPlus + ExBody humanoid imitation policies.
control_architecture: Latent-skill-space VAE-GAN + task-conditioned downstream policy. NVIDIA Isaac Gym implementation.
creator: NVIDIA + Stanford + UC Berkeley + University of Toronto; Xue Bin Peng et al.

notable_capabilities: ancestor of HumanPlus + ExBody humanoid imitation policies
prior_art_notes: ASE (Peng et al. SIGGRAPH 2022) is the canonical successor to AMP (round-21). 3-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: latent-skill-space adversarial-training for character animation, task-conditioned skill reuse. **Direct ancestor of HumanPlus + ExBody humanoid imitation policies** (round-27 entries below). Together with DeepMimic (round-21) + AMP (round-21), establishes the 7-year mocap-imitation-RL chain DeepMimic 2018 → AMP 2021 → ASE 2022 → HumanPlus 2024 → ExBody 2024.

actuator_details: Deployed on Everyday Robots mobile manipulator. The disclosure is the SayCan algorithm: pre-trained large language model (PaLM 540B) provides p(skill|instruction); learned affordance value function provides p(success|skill, observation); their product selects the next skill from a pre-trained skill library.
aliases: Do As I Can, Not As I Say
canonical_name: SayCan (Do As I Can, Not As I Say)
control_architecture: Hierarchical: LLM proposes high-level skills constrained by an affordance value function (RL-trained or BC-trained per-skill success predictor); selected skill is executed by a low-level learned policy. Combines language reasoning with robot-grounded affordances.
creator: Google Robotics + Everyday Robots (Ahn et al.)

(Google + Everyday Robots).

Anticipates: (1) the architectural pattern of LLM language scoring × learned affordance scoring for hierarchical task planning — directly relevant to claims on language-grounded humanoid task planners (every modern 'speak-to-the-robot' product, from Tesla Optimus demos to Figure 02 OpenAI integration, descends from this); (2) the value-function-as-affordance grounding mechanism — relevant to claims on grounded language-to-action mappings; (3) the explicit decoupling of language reasoning (open-vocabulary) from low-level policy (closed-set skills) — relevant to modular VLA architectures. Heavily cited (>1500 citations); arXiv April 2022. Modern claims on 'language-conditioned long-horizon humanoid task planning' face this 4-year-deep 102 anchor.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, evaluated on D4RL Maze2D, locomotion (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2D), and KUKA block-stacking. Trains a diffusion model jointly over state-action trajectories; classifier guidance steers planning toward arbitrary reward, goal, or constraint specifications.
control_architecture: diffusion-model trajectory generator: train denoising network on demonstration trajectories; sample new trajectories by reverse-process denoising with optional gradient guidance from a learned reward classifier. Replanning at each timestep gives MPC-style behavior.
creator: Michael Janner, Yilun Du, Joshua Tenenbaum, Sergey Levine, MIT/UC Berkeley
disclosure_citation: Janner, Michael, Du, Yilun, Tenenbaum, Joshua B., Levine, Sergey. 'Planning with Diffusion for Flexible Behavior Synthesis.' Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2022), Baltimore, July 2022; arXiv:2205.09991, May 2022.
notable_capabilities: compositional task specification at sample time
prior_art_notes: Janner Diffuser is the foundational academic disclosure of trajectory-level diffusion as a planner/policy substrate for robotic control, predating Chi et al.'s Diffusion Policy by ~6 months. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on diffusion models trained over state-action trajectories for robotic motion generation — Diffuser discloses the joint state-action trajectory diffusion architecture; (2) claims on classifier-guided sample-time reward/goal conditioning — Diffuser discloses gradient-guided sampling for arbitrary objective composition; (3) claims on receding-horizon diffusion replanning (MPC-style) — Diffuser discloses replan-each-step. >1500 citations; ICML 2022 proceedings and arXiv timestamped. Modern humanoid diffusion-policy IP claims face this 4-year-deep anchor — and importantly Diffuser predates the modern diffusion-policy boom and discloses generic trajectory diffusion before manipulator-specific patents filed in 2023+.
sources: Janner, M., Du, Y., Tenenbaum, J. B., Levine, S. 'Planning with Diffusion for Flexible Behavior Synthesis.' ICML 2022; arXiv:2205.09991.

actuator_details: 1.18B-parameter Transformer trained as a single model across 604 tasks spanning Atari games, captioning, dialogue, and Sawyer-arm robotic block stacking. Tokenized everything (text, images, button presses, joint torques) into a single sequence.
control_architecture: Single decoder-only Transformer with universal-tokenizer interface; same weights for vision-language tasks and continuous-control robotic tasks. The unified-tokenization-and-shared-weights approach is the architectural disclosure.
creator: DeepMind (Reed et al.)
disclosure_citation: Reed, Scott et al. 'A Generalist Agent.' Transactions on Machine Learning Research, November 2022. arXiv:2205.06175, May 12, 2022. (DeepMind).

universal tokenization of action and observation
prior_art_notes: Gato is the canonical academic disclosure of a generalist agent that unifies vision-language reasoning and continuous robotic control under a single Transformer policy. Anticipates: (1) universal-tokenization of robot actions and visual observations into a single autoregressive sequence — directly relevant to claims on multi-modal VLA models that handle both perception and action via shared weights; (2) cross-embodiment policy training (Sawyer arm + Atari + dialogue under one model) — relevant to multi-embodiment foundation-model claims (RoboCat, Open X-Embodiment, OpenVLA all descend from this thesis); (3) the demonstration that a single moderate-scale Transformer can drive disparate physical and digital tasks — anticipates 'one model, many bodies' patent claims. Published TMLR + arXiv with code partially released. Modern multi-embodiment humanoid IP faces this 4-year-deep anchor.
sensing: RGB camera, joint state, language input (depending on task)
sources: Reed, S. et al. 'A Generalist Agent.' TMLR 2022; arXiv:2205.06175.

actuator_details: Successor to OceanOne with depth extended from 200 m to 1000 m. Glass-sphere syntactic-foam buoyancy modules. Pressure-tolerant electronics in oil-filled compartments at full operating depth. 8-thruster vectored layout retained from OceanOne baseline. Anthropomorphic arms re-engineered with pressure-tolerant joints (no rigid pressure hull on the arms; oil-filled actuator compartments).
control_architecture: Bilateral haptic teleoperation via Sigma.7 + Stanford whole-body operational-space framework. Tether for primary control + power at 1 km depth.
creator: Stanford Robotics Laboratory; Khatib group; expanded design team
disclosure_citation: Khatib, O., Brantner, G., Yeh, X., Salisbury, S. et al. 'OceanOneK: A 1000-meter-depth, bimanual underwater humanoid for archeology and marine exploration'. Science Robotics 2022 (announced July 2022). Subsequent IEEE RA-L publications detail control and pressure-hull innovations.
end_effector: 2× anthropomorphic 7-DoF pressure-tolerant arms with 3-finger underactuated grippers; F/T sensing
notable_capabilities: pressure-tolerant arms (oil-filled, no rigid pressure hull on appendages)
first 1 km depth bimanual humanoid manipulation
deployed for Mediterranean shipwreck archeology (Italy 2022, France 2023)
power_source: surface-supplied via 1 km tether + onboard battery backup
prior_art_notes: OceanOneK extends the OceanOne lineage to 1000 m depth and adds pressure-tolerant oil-filled-actuator art. Directly shields any commercial humanoid AUV claim on: deep-depth (>500 m) bimanual humanoid manipulation, pressure-tolerant joint actuation (no rigid pressure hull on appendages), and integration of Khatib's 38-year operational-space framework with deep underwater manipulation. A 3-year-deep open-academic prior art chain with full element-by-element technical disclosure.
sensing: stereo HD cameras (pressure-tolerant housings), multibeam imaging sonar, depth pressure, IMU, DVL, USBL, wrist F/T
sources: BBC, Le Monde, IEEE Spectrum coverage of Mediterranean shipwreck operations 2022-2023.

actuator_details: 12 ANYdrive series-elastic rotary actuators with integrated harmonic-drive reduction (~50:1) and torque-controlled SEA spring; force-controllable joints with proprioceptive contact estimation. Improved torque envelope vs ANYmal-C; ingress protection IP67 for industrial inspection.
control_architecture: Reinforcement-learning blind+perceptive locomotion policies trained in Isaac Gym/Sim, deployed via teacher-student distillation (Miki Sci.Rob. 2022) and parkour-style high-skill policies (Hoeller Sci.Rob. 2024); on-board state estimation via factor-graph proprioceptive-LiDAR fusion.
creator: ANYbotics AG / ETH Zürich Robotic Systems Lab (Marco Hutter)
disclosure_citation: ANYbotics product disclosure ANYmal D, September 2022; technical updates in Miki, Takahiro et al. 'Learning robust perceptive locomotion for quadrupedal robots in the wild.' Science Robotics 7(62), 2022; Hoeller, David et al. 'ANYmal Parkour: Learning agile navigation for quadrupedal robots.' Science Robotics 9(88), 2024.
notable_capabilities: perceptive RL locomotion deployed in production
prior_art_notes: ANYmal-D is the production-deployed industrial quadruped of the 2022-2024 period and the platform for the headline RSL/ANYbotics RL-locomotion papers in Science Robotics. It anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on perceptive-locomotion RL policies trained in simulation and transferred to outdoor industrial terrain — Miki Sci.Rob. 2022 publishes the teacher-student distillation pipeline running on this hardware; (2) claims on agile parkour-class learned locomotion — Hoeller Sci.Rob. 2024 publishes the policy on ANYmal-D; (3) claims on series-elastic torque-controlled quadruped joints in IP67 industrial enclosures — ANYdrive disclosed at IROS 2018 with hardware refresh on D-variant. Modern legged-robot IP claims face this timestamped industrial-deployment anchor.
sensing: depth cameras (front+rear), 360° LiDAR, IMU, joint torque, foot-contact estimation

Hoeller, D. et al. 'ANYmal Parkour.' Science Robotics 9(88), 2024.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure: cross-attention encoder-decoder Transformer accepting interleaved image and text tokens as 'multimodal prompt.' Trained on 650k expert trajectories across 17 task families in the VIMA-Bench simulator.
canonical_name: VIMA (General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts)
control_architecture: Object-centric attention over a multimodal prompt (e.g., 'put the [IMG_REDBLOCK] on the [IMG_GREENBOWL]'). Action is end-effector pose (pick + place). Cross-attention enables one-shot generalization to novel objects specified at inference via image tokens.
creator: Stanford + NVIDIA + UT Austin (Jiang, Gupta, Zhang, Wang, Dou, Chen, Fei-Fei, Anandkumar, Zhu, Fan)
disclosure_citation: Jiang, Yunfan, Gupta, Agrim, Zhang, Zichen, Wang, Guanzhi, Dou, Yongqiang, Chen, Yanjun, Fei-Fei, Li, Anandkumar, Anima, Zhu, Yuke, Fan, Linxi (Jim). 'VIMA: General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts.' arXiv:2210.03094, October 6, 2022. ICML 2023.
notable_capabilities: one-shot generalization to novel objects via image tokens
prior_art_notes: VIMA is the foundational academic disclosure of multimodal-prompt-conditioned robotic policies, where novel objects can be specified inline via image tokens. Anticipates: (1) interleaved-image-and-text prompts as a generalization mechanism for manipulation policies — directly relevant to claims on humanoid policies that accept image-grounded instructions; (2) cross-attention object-centric task specification — relevant to claims on attention-based VLA models; (3) one-shot novel-object handling at inference via image tokens — relevant to test-time-flexibility manipulation IP. arXiv October 2022, ICML 2023. Code, models, and benchmark publicly released under permissive license. Modern humanoid claims on 'show-the-robot-an-image-and-it-handles-the-novel-object' face this 3.5-year-deep 102 anchor.
sensing: RGB camera, language input, image-token-conditioned prompt
sources: Jiang, Y. et al. 'VIMA: General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts.' ICML 2023; arXiv:2210.03094.

actuator_details: Demonstrated on Everyday Robots mobile manipulators (7-DOF arm + parallel-jaw gripper, mobile base). Architecture is a 35M-parameter Transformer that maps (image_history, language_instruction) → discretized end-effector + base actions tokenized at 256 bins per dimension.
control_architecture: Vision-language transformer policy: input is 6 RGB image history + natural language instruction; output is 11-DOF tokenized action (7 arm + 3 base + 1 mode). Trained on 130k episodes / 700+ tasks collected over 17 months on 13 robots. 3Hz inference rate.

notable_capabilities: zero-shot generalization to novel object configurations
scaling-law demonstration for robotic foundation models
prior_art_notes: RT-1 is the foundational academic disclosure of large-scale Transformer-based vision-language-action policy for real robot control, predating RT-2 (2023) and OpenVLA (2024). Anticipates with full architectural specificity: (1) tokenized action space for cross-task transformer policies — directly relevant to claims on action-tokenization in modern VLAs (Tesla Optimus, Figure 02, 1X NEO, Physical Intelligence π-zero all employ derivatives); (2) language-conditioned manipulation policy with multi-image history — relevant to instruction-following manipulation IP; (3) the data-scaling law showing performance vs. dataset size for robot policies — relevant to claims on data-driven policy training. Code and data partially released under permissive licenses; arXiv preprint available since December 2022. Brohan et al. paper foundational for the entire VLA lineage.
sources: Brohan, A. et al. 'RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale.' arXiv:2212.06817, 2022.

actuator_details: **Billion-scale self-supervised dense temporal-spatial 7-DoF grasp perception**. Successor to GraspNet-1Billion (round-42). Robust to depth noise, real-world clutter, and scene-changes across time. Demonstrates grasp generation on real robot platforms achieving >90% success on novel objects. State-of-the-art Chinese academic grasp-perception benchmark.
control_architecture: Deep-learning-based; self-supervised; trained on GraspNet-1Billion data.
creator: Shanghai Jiao Tong University Lu Cewu Lab; Hao-Shu Fang et al.
disclosure_citation: Fang, H.-S., Wang, C., Fang, H., Gou, M., Liu, J., Yan, H., Liu, W., Xie, Y., Lu, C. 'AnyGrasp: Robust and Efficient Grasp Perception in Spatial and Temporal Domains'. IEEE Transactions on Robotics 39(5), 2023. arXiv:2212.08333. Shanghai Jiao Tong University Lu Cewu Lab.
notable_capabilities: billion-scale self-supervised dense temporal-spatial 7-DoF grasp perception (2023)
robust to depth noise + real-world clutter + scene-changes
prior_art_notes: AnyGrasp (Fang / Lu SJTU T-RO 2023, arXiv 2212.08333) is the state-of-the-art Chinese academic grasp-perception benchmark. 2-year-deep open-permissive prior art. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim deriving from billion-scale self-supervised grasp perception or temporal-spatial 7-DoF grasp generation. Lineage descends from GraspNet-1Billion (round-42) and Dex-Net (round-42).

actuator_details: World-model RL algorithm: learns a recurrent state-space model (RSSM) of the environment, then trains a policy via RL within the imagination of the world model. DreamerV3 demonstrated cross-domain generalization across 150+ Atari, DMLab, MineRL, and continuous-control benchmarks with a single set of hyperparameters.
control_architecture: model-based RL: world model (RSSM) + actor + critic, all trained jointly. Imagination rollouts in the learned world model substitute for real-environment rollouts.
creator: Danijar Hafner, Jurgis Pasukonis, Jimmy Ba, Timothy Lillicrap; Google DeepMind, University of Toronto
disclosure_citation: Hafner, Danijar; Pasukonis, Jurgis; Ba, Jimmy; Lillicrap, Timothy. 'Mastering diverse domains through world models'. arXiv:2301.04104, January 10, 2023. Earlier Dreamer (Hafner et al. 2019/2020) at arXiv:1912.01603.
notable_capabilities: cross-domain generalization with single hyperparameter set across 150+ benchmarks
prior_art_notes: Dreamer V3 (2023) is one of the strongest academic disclosures of model-based RL for cross-domain generalization. Anticipates: (1) world-model RL (RSSM) as the policy-learning substrate for humanoid platforms — relevant to modern model-based humanoid IP; (2) imagination-rollout-based policy training — relevant to claims on data-efficient humanoid RL; (3) cross-domain generalization without per-task hyperparameter tuning — relevant to platform-agnostic humanoid policy IP. The 2023 arXiv preprint plus the open-source DreamerV3 reference implementation provide deep prior art coverage. Modern world-model-based humanoid IP face this 3-year academic anchor.
sources: Hafner, D. et al. 'Mastering diverse domains through world models'. arXiv:2301.04104, 2023.
Hafner, D. et al. 'Dream to control'. arXiv:1912.01603, ICLR 2020 (predecessor).

actuator_details: **Modular framework for NeRF development + the Nerfacto model**. Apache-2.0 open-source. Supports rapid experimentation: GUI viewer + standardized pipeline + 20+ pre-implemented NeRF variants. **Nerfacto** is Nerfstudio's default integrated NeRF model — combines best practices from Mip-NeRF, Instant-NGP, NeRF-W into a robust general-purpose NeRF. The de facto open-academic NeRF research platform.
control_architecture: Modular Python pipeline + Web GUI viewer + Apache-2.0 SDK.
creator: UC Berkeley AI Research (BAIR); Matthew Tancik, Ethan Weber, Angjoo Kanazawa et al.
disclosure_citation: Tancik, M., Weber, E., Ng, E., Li, R., Yi, B., Wang, T., Kristoffersen, A., Austin, J., Salahi, K., Ahuja, A., McAllister, D., Kanazawa, A. 'Nerfstudio: A Modular Framework for Neural Radiance Field Development'. SIGGRAPH 2023. arXiv:2302.04264. UC Berkeley AI Research (BAIR) + UC Berkeley + Stanford.
notable_capabilities: the de facto open-academic NeRF platform
prior_art_notes: Nerfstudio + Nerfacto (Tancik et al. SIGGRAPH 2023) is the canonical open-academic NeRF research framework. 2-year-deep open-permissive prior art. Direct successor to NeRF (round-28) in the open-source NeRF tooling chain. Used in 100+ academic papers as the standard NeRF research substrate. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on NeRF-based scene representation development tooling.
sensing: multi-view RGB + camera poses + optional depth

actuator_details: Vision-language contrastive model trained with **sigmoid loss** (rather than CLIP's softmax loss). Enables much larger batch sizes without quadratic memory cost, leading to faster training and stronger zero-shot performance. The default vision-language encoder for many modern VLAs (e.g., OpenVLA uses SigLIP + DINOv2).
control_architecture: Provides aligned vision + text embeddings for downstream open-vocabulary perception, retrieval, and policy conditioning.
creator: Google Research; Zhai, Mustafa, Kolesnikov, Beyer
disclosure_citation: Zhai, X., Mustafa, B., Kolesnikov, A., Beyer, L. 'Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training'. arXiv:2303.15343, March 2023. ICCV 2023. Google Research.
notable_capabilities: sigmoid loss enables large-batch contrastive training
faster training than CLIP at equivalent quality
open weights via HuggingFace google/siglip-* family
the standard text-encoder for VLA / VLM systems
prior_art_notes: SigLIP is the canonical sigmoid-loss vision-language foundation model (Google ICCV 2023). 2-year-deep prior art for: sigmoid-loss contrastive vision-language training, large-batch-friendly training regime. The text-encoder backbone in OpenVLA, RADIO-ViPE, and many VLA systems. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on open-vocabulary text-image alignment for instruction following.
sources: Zhai et al. arXiv:2303.15343 March 2023; ICCV 2023.

actuator_details: First system to embed CLIP language features into a NeRF radiance field, enabling open-vocabulary 3D scene queries. The architectural ancestor of LEGS (Berkeley AUTOLab IROS 2024) and the entire language-embedded-Gaussian-splatting lineage that followed. ICCV 2023 Oral. CC-BY 4.0 / open-source.
control_architecture: Provides language-grounded 3D scene representation.
creator: UC Berkeley AUTOLab + BAIR; Kerr, Kim, Goldberg, Kanazawa, Tancik
disclosure_citation: Kerr, J., Kim, C. M., Goldberg, K., Kanazawa, A., Tancik, M. 'LERF: Language Embedded Radiance Fields'. arXiv:2303.09553, March 2023. ICCV 2023 (Oral). UC Berkeley AUTOLab + Berkeley AI Research.
notable_capabilities: open-vocabulary 3D scene queries via natural-language text
the architectural ancestor of LEGS, LEG-SLAM, LEGO-SLAM
prior_art_notes: LERF is the canonical first language-embedded NeRF (Berkeley + BAIR, ICCV 2023 Oral). 2-year-deep prior art for: CLIP-embedded 3D radiance fields, open-vocabulary natural-language 3D scene queries. The architectural ancestor of LEGS (round-12), LEG-SLAM (round-12), LEGO-SLAM (round-12), and any commercial claim on language-queryable 3D scene representations. Predates the Gaussian-splatting instantiations and establishes the architectural pattern.
sources: Kerr et al. arXiv:2303.09553 March 2023; ICCV 2023.

actuator_details: **Foundation model for embodied AI vision**. MAE-pretrained Vision Transformer trained on a curated mix of egocentric videos (Ego4D) + manipulation videos + navigation videos + ImageNet. Two model sizes: VC-1-B (200M params) and VC-1-L (300M params). Demonstrates strong frozen-feature performance across 17 embodied AI tasks (manipulation, navigation, locomotion). **The architectural ancestor of subsequent embodied-vision-foundation-model papers** — analog to ImageNet-pretrained ViT for embodied AI.
control_architecture: MAE-pretrained ViT; provides frozen visual features for downstream embodied policies.
creator: Meta AI + UC Berkeley + Georgia Tech; Arjun Majumdar, Karmesh Yadav, Pieter Abbeel, Jitendra Malik et al.
disclosure_citation: Majumdar, A., Yadav, K., Arnaud, S., Ma, J., Chen, C., Silwal, S., Jain, A., Berges, V.-P., Abbeel, P., Malik, J., Batra, D., Lin, Y., Maksymets, O., Rajeswaran, A., Meier, F. 'Where are we in the search for an Artificial Visual Cortex for Embodied Intelligence?'. NeurIPS 2023. arXiv:2303.18240. Meta AI + UC Berkeley + Georgia Tech.
notable_capabilities: first foundation vision model for embodied AI at scale
trained on egocentric videos + manipulation + navigation + ImageNet
prior_art_notes: VC-1 (Majumdar et al. Meta NeurIPS 2023) is the canonical foundation vision model for embodied AI. 2-year-deep open-permissive prior art. Direct architectural ancestor of: subsequent embodied-vision foundation models, NVIDIA AM-RADIO (round-13), DexMV (round-17 entry — egocentric-video-trained manipulation policies). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on embodied-vision foundation models.

actuator_details: 562B-parameter Transformer combining PaLM language model with ViT vision encoder. Continuous observations (images, robot states) are projected into the language token embedding space and concatenated with text tokens before the Transformer. Trained on mixed corpora of robot trajectories and internet-scale vision-language data.
control_architecture: End-to-end multimodal: image+state observations and language instructions are co-tokenized; the model outputs natural-language plans or directly commands a low-level policy. Demonstrates positive transfer from internet vision-language data to robotic task performance.
creator: Google Robotics + TU Berlin (Driess et al.)
disclosure_citation: Driess, Danny et al. 'PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model.' arXiv:2303.03378, March 6, 2023. International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) 2023. Authors: Driess, D., Xia, F., Sajjadi, M.S.M., Lynch, C., Chowdhery, A., Ichter, B., Wahid, A., Tompson, J., Vuong, Q., Yu, T., Huang, W., Chebotar, Y., Sermanet, P., Duckworth, D., Levine, S., Vanhoucke, V., Hausman, K., Toussaint, M., Greff, K., Zeng, A., Mordatch, I., Florence, P. (Google + TU Berlin).
notable_capabilities: positive transfer from internet vision-language to robotic tasks
prior_art_notes: PaLM-E is the canonical academic disclosure of large multimodal embodied language models with internet-pretraining transfer to robotic tasks. Anticipates: (1) embedding continuous robot observations into language-model token space for unified processing — directly relevant to claims on multimodal humanoid policies that incorporate proprioception and vision in a shared transformer; (2) demonstration that internet-scale vision-language pretraining transfers positively to robot manipulation — relevant to claims on 'foundation-model'-style humanoid IP; (3) single-model architecture spanning planning and execution — relevant to monolithic-VLA claims. Heavily cited (>1000 citations); arXiv March 2023. Modern humanoid VLA claims face this 3-year-deep anchor on multimodal-token-space embedding.
sources: Driess, D. et al. 'PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model.' ICML 2023; arXiv:2303.03378.

actuator_details: Visuomotor policy: a denoising diffusion model that takes RGB observations and outputs a sequence of future actions. Trained on demonstrated trajectories. Multi-modal action distribution capability (a key advantage over deterministic regression).
control_architecture: denoising diffusion model (CNN or transformer backbone) generates action sequences given visual context. Action chunking (10-16 step horizon) for stability. CFG-style guidance for goal conditioning.
creator: Cheng Chi, Siyuan Feng, Yilun Du, Zhenjia Xu, Eric Cousineau, Benjamin Burchfiel, Shuran Song; Columbia University, Toyota Research Institute
disclosure_citation: Chi, C., Feng, S., Du, Y., Xu, Z., Cousineau, E., Burchfiel, B., Song, S. 'Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion'. arXiv:2303.04137, March 9, 2023; Robotics: Science and Systems 2023.
end_effector: depends on training data; typical: parallel jaw gripper, dual-arm
notable_capabilities: multi-modal action distribution learning from demonstrations
prior_art_notes: Diffusion Policy is one of the foundational academic disclosures of generative-model action policies for robotics. Anticipates: (1) diffusion models as the policy class for robotic manipulation — directly relevant to modern claims on generative-model humanoid policies (Pi-Zero, Π0, OpenVLA all build on or extend this); (2) action chunking as a stability technique — relevant to claims on chunked-action humanoid IP; (3) multi-modal action distribution learning — relevant to claims on robust-to-demonstration-variability humanoid policies. The 2023 RSS paper and open-source code release provide extensive prior art coverage.
sources: Chi, C. et al. 'Diffusion Policy'. arXiv:2303.04137 (RSS 2023).

actuator_details: Self-supervised vision foundation model. Trained on 142M curated images via image-level + patch-level self-distillation losses. Produces high-quality dense per-pixel features without supervision. ViT backbone in S/B/L/g sizes. The standard self-supervised vision encoder for modern robotic perception.
control_architecture: Provides dense per-pixel features for downstream perception (segmentation, depth, monocular depth via DPT heads, embedding-based SLAM).
creator: Meta AI Research (FAIR); Oquab, Darcet, Moutakanni et al.
disclosure_citation: Oquab, M., Darcet, T., Moutakanni, T., Vo, H., Szafraniec, M., Khalidov, V., Fernandez, P., Haziza, D., Massa, F., El-Nouby, A., et al. 'DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision'. arXiv:2304.07193, April 2023. Meta AI Research (FAIR). Apache-2.0 release.
notable_capabilities: backbone in OpenVLA, LEG-SLAM, many other systems
prior_art_notes: DINOv2 is the canonical Meta self-supervised vision foundation model (April 2023). 2-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: self-supervised dense visual features at scale, ViT-g-class image encoders for robotics. The vision encoder in OpenVLA, LEG-SLAM, and many other systems in the corpus. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on self-supervised onboard visual feature learning.

actuator_details: ALOHA hardware: low-cost ($20K BOM) bimanual teleoperation rig with two Trossen WidowX-7 leader arms and two follower arms. ACT software: action-chunking transformer policy.
control_architecture: ACT policy: transformer that takes RGB observations and outputs action chunks (50 steps); trained on bimanual teleoperation demonstrations via behavior cloning.
creator: Tony Zhao, Vikash Kumar, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn; Stanford University and Google DeepMind
disclosure_citation: Zhao, T., Kumar, V., Levine, S., Finn, C. 'Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware'. arXiv:2304.13705, April 23, 2023; Robotics: Science and Systems 2023.
notable_capabilities: imitation learning from <50 demos for many tasks
prior_art_notes: ACT/ALOHA is the foundational academic disclosure of low-cost bimanual teleoperation hardware paired with action-chunking transformer policy. Anticipates: (1) bimanual teleoperation via leader-follower arm pairs — relevant to claims on cost-efficient bimanual humanoid teleoperation IP; (2) action-chunking transformer policy for fine-grained manipulation — relevant to claims on chunked-action humanoid policies; (3) <$20K bimanual hardware as a reference platform — relevant to commercial bimanual IP for sub-$20K humanoid arms. The April 2023 release with full open-source hardware design + software unblocked widespread bimanual learning research.
sensing: four RGB cameras (head, two wrists, top); joint encoders
sources: Zhao, T. et al. 'Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware'. arXiv:2304.13705, RSS 2023.

actuator_details: Amphibious member of the STAR family. Adds **water-driving capability** via wheel-paddle hybrid ground contact patches. 3.5 m/s on land, 1.5 m/s in water. Sealed enclosure for amphibious operation. Sprawl-tuning + leg reconfiguration carried over from RSTAR. Limited obstacle-climbing in this variant (the priority was the aquatic-terrestrial transition).
control_architecture: Pre-programmed mode-switching between terrestrial and aquatic locomotion. Operator selects mode pre-mission.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; Avi Cohen, David Zarrouk
disclosure_citation: Cohen, A., Zarrouk, D. 'AmphiSTAR: A High-Speed Amphibious Reconfigurable Robot'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 2023; ICRA 2023 demo. Ben-Gurion University, Zarrouk lab.
end_effector: wheel-paddle hybrid contact patches (terrestrial wheels double as aquatic paddles)
notable_capabilities: first STAR-family member to operate in water
prior_art_notes: AmphiSTAR establishes 3-year-deep open-academic prior art for **terrestrial-aquatic transition in a single platform with shared ground-contact mechanism**. Directly relevant to free-humanoid-submersible (and the centaur's wetland mode-transition) — proves that wheel-paddle hybrid contact patches and sealed-enclosure amphibious operation are well-anticipated open art. Any commercial claim on amphibious humanoid robotics faces this lineage plus the deeper aquatic-robotics chain (Slocum/Seaglider, OceanOne, AmphiSTAR).
sensing: IMU + depth pressure sensor; camera optional
sources: Cohen, A., Zarrouk, D. IEEE RA-L 2023.

actuator_details: **Real-world long-horizon manipulation benchmark for furniture assembly**. Standardized IKEA-style furniture pieces with fiducial markers. **8 furniture models × 9 assembly tasks**, graduated difficulty. Provides a reproducible real-world (not simulated) benchmark for assembly-class manipulation tasks. Distinct from sim-only benchmarks (RLBench, robomimic, LIBERO, RoboCasa) by real-world deployment. Open-source assembly + task-script library.
control_architecture: Standardized real-robot evaluation protocol; reproducible across labs.
creator: KAIST + USC; Minho Heo, Youngwoon Lee, Doohyun Lee, Joseph J. Lim
disclosure_citation: Heo, M., Lee, Y., Lee, D., Lim, J. J. 'FurnitureBench: Reproducible Real-World Benchmark for Long-Horizon Complex Manipulation'. RSS 2023. arXiv:2305.12821. KAIST + USC.
prior_art_notes: FurnitureBench is the canonical real-world long-horizon manipulation benchmark (Heo et al. RSS 2023). 2-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: furniture-assembly real-robot benchmark, fiducial-based standardization for cross-lab reproducibility. Distinct architectural branch from sim-only benchmarks: FurnitureBench is real-robot, while RLBench/robomimic/LIBERO/RoboCasa are simulated. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on furniture-assembly or long-horizon real-world benchmark performance.
sensing: standardized fiducial markers + RGB cameras + force/torque

actuator_details: **Lifelong robot learning benchmark** — 130 manipulation tasks across four suites: LIBERO-Spatial (spatial-knowledge transfer), LIBERO-Object (object-knowledge transfer), LIBERO-Goal (goal-knowledge transfer), and LIBERO-100 (entangled knowledge across 100 tasks). Built on the SAPIEN simulator. Extendible procedural generation pipeline that can generate infinitely many tasks. MIT-licensed.
control_architecture: Provides task suite + standard baseline policies for IL/RL evaluation.
creator: UT Austin + Bytedance Research; Bo Liu, Yifeng Zhu, Yuke Zhu, Peter Stone et al.
disclosure_citation: Liu, B., Zhu, Y., Gao, C., Feng, Y., Liu, Q., Zhu, Y., Stone, P. 'LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning'. NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks. arXiv:2306.03310. UT Austin + Bytedance Research.
notable_capabilities: the canonical 2024-2025 VLA evaluation benchmark (OpenVLA-OFT, π₀, RDT-1B all report LIBERO success rates)
prior_art_notes: LIBERO is the canonical lifelong-robot-learning benchmark (Liu et al. NeurIPS 2023). 2-year-deep prior art on the benchmark surface that **OpenVLA-OFT (round-12), π₀ (round-12), RDT-1B (round-13), and most contemporary VLA papers report results against**. Any commercial humanoid VLA claim of 'we outperform X% on LIBERO' implies the LIBERO benchmark itself is reproducible academic art — that benchmark's 130 tasks plus extendible generation pipeline are 100% open-permissive prior art. Together with robomimic (round-16) and SimplerEnv (round-17 entry), establishes the open-academic VLA evaluation substrate.

actuator_details: Multi-embodiment generalist policy demonstrated on 4 different robot arms (KUKA, Sawyer, Panda, etc.) with different gripper types. Self-improvement loop: deploy RoboCat → collect data on new task → retrain → deploy again. Trained on 22 robotic tasks spanning multiple embodiments.
control_architecture: Visual Goal-Conditioned Policy (VGCP) Transformer that accepts an image goal + current observation; trained on collected demonstrations with self-generated additional data (model-collected then filtered) used to bootstrap further training.
creator: DeepMind (Bousmalis et al.)
disclosure_citation: Bousmalis, Konstantinos et al. 'RoboCat: A Self-Improving Generalist Agent for Robotic Manipulation.' arXiv:2306.11706, June 20, 2023. Transactions on Machine Learning Research, 2024. Authors: Bousmalis, K., Vezzani, G., Rao, D., Devin, C., Lee, A.X., Bauza, M., Davchev, T., Zhou, Y., Gupta, A., Raju, A., Laurens, A., Fantacci, C., Dalibard, V., Zambelli, M., Martins, M., Pevceviciute, R., Blokzijl, M., Denil, M., Batchelor, N., Lampe, T., Parisotto, E., Zolna, K., Reed, S., Colmenarejo, S.G., Scholz, J., Abdolmaleki, A., Groth, O., Regli, J-B., Sushkov, O., Rothorl, T., Chen, J.E., Aytar, Y., Barker, D., Ortiz, J., Riedmiller, M., Springenberg, J.T., Hadsell, R., Nori, F., Heess, N. (DeepMind).
end_effector: varied: parallel-jaw gripper, three-finger gripper, etc., across embodiments
notable_capabilities: few-shot adaptation to new tasks via fine-tuning
prior_art_notes: RoboCat is the canonical academic disclosure of self-improving multi-embodiment generalist robotic policies. Anticipates: (1) the cross-embodiment training loop where one model generalizes across distinct robot platforms — directly relevant to claims on humanoid policies trained on heterogeneous robot data (a core selling point of every commercial humanoid VLA); (2) self-collected-data improvement loop — relevant to autonomous-data-flywheel claims (Tesla Dojo + Optimus, Figure's data pipeline); (3) image-goal-conditioned policy as a unified interface — relevant to goal-image-conditioned manipulation IP. Published TMLR + arXiv June 2023; partial code release. Modern humanoid 'data flywheel' patent claims face this anchor.
sensing: RGB camera, proprioception, optional image goal
sources: Bousmalis, K. et al. 'RoboCat: A Self-Improving Generalist Agent.' TMLR 2024; arXiv:2306.11706.

actuator_details: deployed on multiple manipulator platforms
control_architecture: VLA model leveraging vision-language pretraining for manipulation
creator: Google DeepMind
disclosure_citation: Brohan, A. et al. 'RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control.' arXiv 2307.15818, July 2023.
notable_capabilities: transfer of web-pretrained knowledge to manipulation
notes: DeepMind has published the RT-1, RT-2, and RT-X series openly via arXiv, making them strong commons assets.
prior_art_notes: RT-2 is foundational publicly-disclosed prior art for VLA architectures applied to robotics. Any subsequent VLA patent claim must contend with this disclosure.

actuator_details: Six robot embodiments (Franka Panda, UR5, Flexiv Rizon, KUKA iiwa14, Jaka Zu5, etc.) operating across 147 tasks; >110k human-teleoperated episodes spanning >50TB raw multi-modal data. Each episode synchronizes RGB-D, audio, force-torque, tactile, and human-demonstration video.
control_architecture: data substrate for imitation/policy learning; not itself a controller. Episodes labelled with natural-language task descriptors, success annotations, and matched human-demonstration video.
creator: Hao-Shu Fang et al., Shanghai Jiao Tong University Machine Vision and Intelligence Group
disclosure_citation: Fang, Hao-Shu, Fang, Hongjie, Tang, Zhenyu, Liu, Jirong, Wang, Junbo, Zhu, Haoyi, Lu, Cewu. 'RH20T: A Comprehensive Robotic Dataset for Learning Diverse Skills in One-Shot.' arXiv:2307.00595, July 2023; ICRA 2024 workshop and project release.
prior_art_notes: RH20T is one of the largest publicly-released heterogeneous robot trajectory datasets prior to OpenX-Embodiment. It anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on multi-embodiment imitation learning where a single policy is trained across robots with differing kinematics — RH20T explicitly demonstrates and releases the data substrate; (2) claims on language-annotated demonstration corpora paired with sensor-rich teleoperation — RH20T pairs RGB-D, force-torque, tactile, audio, and matched human-video for each episode; (3) claims on one-shot/few-shot skill acquisition from teleoperated data — the dataset's headline benchmark. Released CC-BY 4.0 with timestamped arXiv and project page; broadly indexed. Modern humanoid imitation-learning IP claims to multi-embodiment trajectory corpora face this 2023 anchor.
sensing: multi-view RGB-D, microphone audio, 6-axis force-torque, tactile
sources: Fang, H.-S. et al. 'RH20T: A Comprehensive Robotic Dataset for Learning Diverse Skills in One-Shot.' arXiv:2307.00595, 2023.

actuator_details: Open-weight large language model family from Meta. 7B / 13B / 70B parameter sizes. **First open-weight LLM at GPT-3.5-class capability**, released under a permissive (though not strictly OSI-open) custom license. The language-model backbone of OpenVLA (round-12 entry) and many other VLA systems.
control_architecture: Provides language understanding + generation substrate for downstream agents, VLAs, and instruction-following policies.
creator: Meta AI; Touvron, Martin, Stone, et al.
disclosure_citation: Touvron, H., Martin, L., Stone, K., et al. 'Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models'. arXiv:2307.09288, July 2023. Meta AI.
prior_art_notes: LLaMA 2 is Meta's canonical open-weight LLM (July 2023). 2-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: 7B-70B-class open-weight language models. The language backbone of OpenVLA — directly anchors the LLM-grounded VLA architectural pattern. Shields any commercial humanoid claim on LLM-grounded instruction following where Llama-class open weights are an architectural alternative.

actuator_details: **RetNet: Retentive Network as Transformer alternative**. Three-fold computational paradigm: parallel + recurrent + chunkwise recurrent. Aims to combine Transformer's training parallelism + recurrent network's inference efficiency. Together with Mamba (round-34), establishes the post-Transformer architecture exploration.
control_architecture: N/A — sequence-modeling architecture.
creator: Microsoft Research + Tsinghua University; Yutao Sun, Furu Wei et al.
disclosure_citation: Sun, Y., Dong, L., Huang, S., Ma, S., Xia, Y., Xue, J., Wang, J., Wei, F. 'Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models'. arXiv:2307.08621, July 2023. Microsoft Research + Tsinghua University.
prior_art_notes: RetNet (Sun et al. Microsoft + Tsinghua 2023) is one of the canonical post-Transformer architecture explorations. 2-year-deep public-domain prior art. Together with Mamba (round-34), establishes the alternative-architecture prior-art chain that challenges Transformer dominance in long-context sequence modeling.

actuator_details: WidowX 250s 6-DoF arm primary platform; supplemented with Franka and other robots in extension subsets. 60,096 demonstration trajectories across 24 environments and 13 skills; teleoperated and scripted-policy generation.
control_architecture: data substrate; benchmarks include RT-1, RT-2, behavior cloning, language-conditioned policy learning. Episodes carry natural-language instruction, RGB observations, joint+gripper actions.
creator: Homer Walke et al., UC Berkeley RAIL / Stanford IRIS

actuator_details: Software framework, not a physical platform. MJX is a pure-JAX reimplementation of the MuJoCo physics engine that runs natively on GPU/TPU via XLA compilation. Supports MJCF model definition, contact dynamics with soft and hard constraints, articulated rigid-body dynamics, and convex friction-cone solvers. Apache-2.0 license. Differentiable end-to-end via JAX autodiff, enabling gradient-based policy optimization and trajectory optimization directly through the simulator. Achieves >10,000 envs in parallel on a single H100.
control_architecture: Provides differentiable physics substrate. Used in DeepMind's locomotion training pipelines (Brax + MJX, OPAL, MaxBPC), in trajectory optimization (cross-entropy MPC, predictive sampling MPC), and in academic RL libraries (Brax, Mujoco Playground). Supports JAX vmap/pmap for SIMD-style vectorized rollouts. MuJoCo's contact model is Featherstone-derived and includes soft-contact regularization unique to the MuJoCo lineage.

actuator_details: Software framework, not a physical platform. Apache-2.0 PyTorch library implementing imitation-learning and reinforcement-learning policies for real-world robots. Supports common low-cost arms (Koch, SO-100, Moss, Aloha bimanual), Stretch mobile manipulator, and Unitree humanoids. Provides unified dataset format (HuggingFace LeRobotDataset) for teleoperated demonstrations and a model-zoo of trained policy checkpoints.
control_architecture: Multi-policy training and evaluation framework. Implements: ACT (Action Chunking Transformer), Diffusion Policy, TDMPC2 (Temporal Difference MPC), VQ-BeT (Vector-Quantized Behavior Transformer), Pi0 / Pi0-FAST (vision-language-action), SmolVLA. Standardizes data loaders, training loops, distributed training (Accelerate), and real-robot inference. Common policy interface allows mixing/matching architectures with datasets.
creator: Remi Cadene and contributors; HuggingFace, Inc. (with extensive academic contributions from Stanford, CMU, NYU, MIT, IIIT-Hyderabad, ETH Zurich research groups via upstream policies)
disclosure_citation: Cadene, Remi et al. 'LeRobot: State-of-the-art AI for real-world robotics in PyTorch.' HuggingFace blog announcement and GitHub repository launch, March 13, 2024 (https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot). Cadene was previously a research engineer at Tesla AI / formerly at FAIR Paris before joining HuggingFace; the LeRobot framework consolidates open-source implementations of policies (ACT, Diffusion Policy, TDMPC, VQ-BeT, Pi0, SmolVLA) and datasets in a unified Apache-2.0 PyTorch substrate.
end_effector: agnostic; supports parallel-jaw and dexterous end-effectors via URDF
notable_capabilities: unified PyTorch substrate for IL/RL robot policies

prior_art_notes: LeRobot (March 2024) is the canonical open-source unified framework for training and deploying imitation-learning and reinforcement-learning robot policies, published Apache-2.0 by HuggingFace. Anticipates with full architectural specificity: (1) multi-policy training and evaluation framework with a common interface — directly relevant to commercial claims on policy-architecture-agnostic VLA training pipelines (1X, Figure, Tesla Optimus, Genesis AI all build training pipelines that resemble this structure); (2) standardized dataset format for teleoperated demonstrations across heterogeneous embodiments (LeRobotDataset) — relevant to claims on cross-embodiment data unification, anticipating Open X-Embodiment-style aggregation patents; (3) the model-zoo pattern (pre-trained policy checkpoints downloadable via the HuggingFace Hub) — relevant to claims on commercial-grade pre-trained robot policy distribution; (4) real-robot inference on commodity hardware via PyTorch — relevant to claims on edge-deployable VLA systems. The Apache-2.0 license combined with extensive third-party contributions (Stanford Aloha team, Princeton Diffusion Policy, NYU/Cycle's TDMPC2, Physical Intelligence Pi0) makes this entry the consolidated prior art anchor for the entire 2024-2026 VLA-training-stack patent space. Modern VLA pipeline IP filings face this 2-year-deep anchor with full source disclosure.

Generalizes across spatial configurations, viewpoints, and embodiments. Used in IROS 2025's Generalizable Humanoid Manipulation paper alongside Open-TeleVision.

actuator_details: Transformer-based diffusion-policy generalist robot policy. Trained on **800k robot trajectories** from a curated 25-dataset subset of the Open X-Embodiment dataset. Demonstrated zero-shot and few-shot transfer across 9 robotic platforms with new observation and action spaces.

Anticipates: (1) the integration of diffusion-policy action heads into transformer-based VLAs — directly relevant to claims on hybrid transformer-diffusion humanoid policies (essentially every 2025+ humanoid policy stack); (2) input-flexible generalist policies that accept any subset of cameras + optional language — relevant to claims on 'plug-and-play' humanoid policies; (3) full open-source weights and training code — establishes a defensive-publication baseline for the entire VLA design space. Code, weights, and training data fully released under Apache 2.0 / permissive licenses. Heavily cited within 18 months. Modern claims on transformer+diffusion-head humanoid policies face this 2-year-deep 102 anchor.
sensing: RGB cameras (1-3 views), proprioception, optional language
sources: Octo Model Team. 'Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy.' RSS 2024; arXiv:2405.12213.

actuator_details: Five-finger 3D-printed anthropomorphic hand. **Antagonistic-tendon mechanism** — agonist + antagonist tendon pairs allow active opening AND closing (classic SoftHand only actively closes; passive return). Two-layer palm design with separate routing for agonist vs. antagonist tendons. Two differential mechanisms enable distinct joint control modes: enclosing grasp vs. fingertip grasp.
control_architecture: Highly underactuated — synergy-driven from a small number of motors (specific count in paper). Tactile feedback via integrated vision-based tactile sensors at fingertips. Dual-tendon active control allows specific joint targeting (DIP vs. PIP).
creator: Bristol Robotics Laboratory (Lepora group) + Pisa-IIT (Bianchi, Catalano)
disclosure_citation: Li, H., Ford, C. J., Lu, C., Lin, Y., Bianchi, M., Catalano, M. G., Psomopoulou, E., Lepora, N. F. 'Tactile SoftHand-A: 3D-Printed, Tactile, Highly-underactuated, Anthropomorphic Robot Hand with an Antagonistic Tendon Mechanism'. arXiv:2406.12731, June 2024. International Journal of Robotics Research, October 2025. Bristol Robotics Laboratory + Pisa-IIT collaboration.
end_effector: five 3D-printed D-type fingers with active antagonism + integrated 3D-printed vision-based tactile sensors
notable_capabilities: antagonistic active open/close (vs. passive-return SoftHand classic)
prior_art_notes: Tactile SoftHand-A is the 2024-2025 direct successor to the Pisa-IIT SoftHand 2 (round-8 entry pisa-iit-softhand-2). Adds antagonistic tendon mechanism (active open + active close), integrated vision-based tactile sensing, and full 3D-printed fabrication. IJRR October 2025. Direct shielding for free-humanoid-platform's hand v0.1 commitments — Tactile SoftHand-A has antagonistic-tendon prior art that the v0.1 hand's passive-return spring approach explicitly is the alternative to. Together with shadow-dexterous-hand, pisa-iit-softhand, dlr-hand-arm-system-2011, and pisa-iit-softhand-2, establishes deep open-academic prior art for anthropomorphic underactuated tendon-driven hand robotics. **Particularly relevant for hand v0.2 design decisions** — the antagonistic-tendon path is well-anticipated open art.
sensing: integrated 3D-printed vision-based tactile sensors at each fingertip; tendon-state proprioception
sources: Li et al. International Journal of Robotics Research October 2025 (DOI: 10.1177/02783649251379516).

actuator_details: **Whole-body humanoid imitation from human motion**. Two-stage approach: (1) train low-level shadowing policy in simulation from human-motion data via RL; (2) collect imitation-learning demonstrations on real humanoid via the policy. Demonstrated on Unitree H1 humanoid (corpus entry unitree-h1). Architectural successor to AMP + ASE motion-imitation lineage applied to actual humanoid hardware.
control_architecture: Two-stage: RL-trained shadowing policy + IL fine-tuning. CoRL 2024.

the architectural anchor of subsequent humanoid-imitation papers
prior_art_notes: HumanPlus (Fu et al. CoRL 2024) is the canonical Stanford humanoid-imitation-from-humans paper. 1-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: two-stage RL-shadowing + IL fine-tuning, real-hardware humanoid full-body imitation from human motion. Direct architectural application of AMP/ASE lineage (rounds 21+27) to actual humanoid hardware. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on 'humanoid imitates humans' or 'mocap-trained humanoid policy on real hardware'.

actuator_details: **DUSt3R successor adding image-matching capability**. Extends DUSt3R's pointmap regression with **dense feature matching** between image pairs. Achieves SOTA on map-free visual localization + relative pose estimation. ECCV 2024 publication.
control_architecture: Transformer pointmap regression + dense feature matching.

Together with DUSt3R (round-28), MegaSaM (round-13), ViPE (round-11), RADIO-ViPE (round-10), establishes the calibration-free reconstruction chain that any commercial humanoid camera-perception claim must contend with.

actuator_details: **Foundational monocular depth estimation foundation model**. V2 successor to Depth Anything V1 (CVPR 2024). Trained on 595K synthetic + 62M unlabeled real images via teacher-student distillation. Achieves SOTA monocular depth estimation across diverse scenes. Multiple model sizes (S/B/L/G). Open weights via HuggingFace LiheYoung/depth-anything-v2.

NeurIPS 2024) is the canonical open monocular depth estimation foundation model. 1-year-deep open-permissive prior art. **Used in NVIDIA ViPE (round-11) + RADIO-ViPE (round-10) as the metric-depth backbone**. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on monocular depth estimation as part of an onboard perception stack.

actuator_details: 7B-parameter VLA built on the Prismatic-7B vision-language model (Llama 2 backbone + DINOv2/SigLIP visual encoders). Trained on 970k episodes from Open X-Embodiment. Action tokenization: each of the 7 action dimensions discretized to 256 bins, written into the LLM vocabulary by overwriting the 256 least-frequently-used Llama tokens.
control_architecture: Autoregressive VLA: image + language → action tokens → continuous actions via discrete-bin decoding. Fine-tunable to new robots/tasks with LoRA; full-parameter fine-tuning supported. Outperforms RT-2-X (55B) at 7B parameters on the Open X-Embodiment benchmark.

actuator_details: Mid-scale humanoid (~1.4 m, ~30 kg target class). In-house-built lightweight design optimized for learning-based control: low simulation complexity, anthropomorphic kinematics, and reliability against falls. Quasi-direct-drive actuators in legs and arms. Specific motor/reducer selection in the public arXiv paper.
control_architecture: Reinforcement-learning locomotion controller trained in simulation with light domain randomization; deployed zero-shot to hardware. Demonstrates narrow sim-to-real gap and robust locomotion across outdoor terrains. The platform is explicitly designed as a research substrate for learning-based control rather than a closed product.

RL controller with zero-shot sim-to-real deployment

actuator_details: Open-source humanoid-teleoperation system using **Apple Vision Pro** as the operator interface. Stereo video from the robot's head streams to the headset (immersive first-person POV); the operator's head + arm + hand pose is mirrored to the robot. Active head tracking (camera twist/tilt) follows operator gaze. Demonstrated on Unitree H1 (with multi-finger hand) and Fourier GR1 (with grippers).

CoRL 2024). 10-month-deep open-permissive prior art for: VR-headset humanoid teleop with first-person stereo POV, active head tracking for gaze-following, hand-pose mirroring across Vision Pro + humanoid arm. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on Apple-Vision-Pro-or-equivalent VR teleop. actuator_details: Language-embedded Gaussian-splatting representation built incrementally by a mobile robot. Each Gaussian primitive carries a CLIP-aligned language feature enabling open-vocabulary scene queries. 3.5× faster training than LERF baseline. Demonstrated on a mobile manipulator (Stretch) building room-scale scene representations.

Predates and informs LEG-SLAM, LEGO-SLAM, and any commercial humanoid claim on language-queryable 3D scene maps built onboard.

actuator_details: **Unified physics-based character control via masked-motion-inpainting**. Masked-token architecture (analogous to BERT/MAE) applied to motion sequences: the policy is trained to inpaint missing motion tokens given partial constraints. Enables **uniform conditioning across many task types** (joint position targets, end-effector targets, contact constraints). Architectural successor to AMP (round-21) + ASE (round-27).
control_architecture: Masked-token motion-inpainting transformer. NVIDIA Isaac Gym training.

notable_capabilities: uniform conditioning across task types (joint, EE, contact)
prior_art_notes: MaskedMimic (Tessler + Peng SIGGRAPH Asia 2024) is the architectural successor to AMP + ASE for physics-based character control. 1-year-deep open-permissive prior art. Continues the DeepMimic 2018 → AMP 2021 → ASE 2022 → MaskedMimic 2024 chain. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on masked-token motion-inpainting or unified-conditioning character control.

actuator_details: Vision-language-action **flow model** for general robot control. Pretrained on diverse multi-robot demonstration data (mobile manipulation, bimanual, single-arm). Single foundation policy controls multiple robot embodiments. Action distribution modeled via flow matching (vs. diffusion or autoregressive). Significant step in unified-VLA-foundation-model lineage post RT-2 / OpenVLA.
control_architecture: Foundation-model policy: pretrained VLA + flow-matching action head + per-embodiment fine-tuning.

Pre-trained on the largest multi-robot demonstration corpus to date and fine-tuned on a 6K+ episode bimanual dataset. Uses diffusion model formulation (vs. flow-matching π₀ or autoregressive RT-2/OpenVLA) for action distribution.

Differentiable bundle adjustment layer iteratively updates scene geometry + camera parameters. Integrates monocular depth priors into training and inference. Uncertainty-aware global BA. The closest predecessor to NVIDIA ViPE — RADIO-ViPE / ViPE explicitly cite MegaSaM as the prior baseline.

the closest predecessor to NVIDIA ViPE
